volumes.description: A Corner of Valivija
volumes.story:
O Nabu Malikata,
Eternal beauty who absolves our sins,
Mother of all inspiration and madness.
Hurry now. Make haste with the wine's bright splendor,
And bloom in scarlet upon my golden cup.

O Nabu Malikata,
Eternal beauty who absolves our sins,
Mother of all inspiration and madness.
The king in red offers you a crown of gold.
Your languid, wine-bright eyes
Unmoor the hearts of lovers.
Divine and intoxicating spirit!
Deaf to the prayers of those who drink.
If I dare weigh your face against the flowering fields,
My heart recoils in shame.
For whosoever gazes upon your likeness
Shall fall into a madness such as mine.

O Nabu Malikata,
Eternal beauty who absolves our sins,
Mother of all inspiration and madness.
However steadfast our devotion,
You give nothing back, and your heart remains unmoved.
But how could the joys of heaven ever belong to the earth?
Ecstasy is hidden in the wine of the rose.
It is only because we are steeped
In your boundless, unending grace,
That we think you have no tenderness at all.

O Nabu Malikata,
Eternal beauty who absolves our sins,
Mother of all inspiration and madness.
The princess in azure skirts knows your secrets.
Come, listen now!
To love, and to life
Carried upon the morning wind through the forest,
Echoing in the cup from which you both drink.
The rose always hides behind its veil.
A nightingale slips into my garden,
Singing of shame and sorrow,
Then takes wing and leaves once more.

name: Note
description: Note

volumes.title: Note
volumes.description: Note
volumes.story:
(Written in two languages. The language used in the upper text is completely unfamiliar.)

Your containment facility is rather ingenious. It took me years of careful tinkering from the inside before I finally managed to slip out, though I trust that will not shock you too much. I may only be a novelist, but I have wandered across many worlds and devoured countless mystery and detective stories, so a sharp mind is practically part of the job.

If you happen to find this note, do relax. The containment vessel should still be intact. I think.

To be honest, the days locked inside were so unbearably dull that I ended up doing something rather productive. I finally worked out the ending to VM. Even so, I must say that what you did was rather unfair. The universe may not share a single code of laws, but locking someone away without so much as an explanation seems a little unreasonable, does it not? You did not even allow the border authorities to speak with me.

So now you tell me I entered illegally. That is rather amusing, given that I have already received royalties in your local currency. By now the publisher (Yae Publishing House, if I have the name right), must have readers searching everywhere for me.

Then again, after all these years, I doubt anyone still cares how the story ends.

This message was written in two languages (the language of the Andromeda Empire and the local tongue). The two scripts are printed together to reduce the chance of misunderstanding.

...The "passage" stands open anew... Time grows brief...
...By the swiftness with which the Abyss seeps into the world, it appears that all contained within the celestial shell shall draw to a close within a few centuries... Rotwang has arrived at a similar conclusion after undertaking his own calculations...
...I fear I must set forth before long. Yet, the plan I have set in motion shall not cease nonetheless...

volumes.title: Notes by a Certain Noble Individual (I)
volumes.description: Notes by a Certain Noble Individual (I)
volumes.story:
The "passage" stands open at last, though the price paid was heavier than I had ever imagined, and the innocent were ensnared as well... I dare not pray for deliverance from the endless torment of the curse, save only that I may be the sole bearer of all sins committed...
...I had deemed that, much like the toxic blood which spewed forth at the opening of the "passage," this place would be inundated by the filth of the Abyss. Only when I stood truly within the shadows did I see that all within was the very reverse of what was transpiring in the world without. In truth, not only was there no toxic, foul blood to be found, but there was nothing of substance at all, save for a fine white dust in the air. It was as though all in existence had long since been ground to dust by the winds. Only when I had walked through that storm, to its very end, did I find that strange castle...
...This place is without doubt that "world of shadow" which I had already visited times without number within my dark and heavy dreams. These are, unquestioned, the ruins of Hyperborea — that lost homeland I had long sought with great pains, yet in vain. Perhaps this is where I may at last find the answer I have pursued, concerning myself, and even all the fae...
...But what has truly taken me by surprise is the discovery that I am not the first to set foot in this place. And, even more wondrous still, the one who had preceded me was a subject with whom I had long been acquainted... We once contended side by side against savage beasts, and together drove the north wind across the winter wastes. Though he seldom attended the feasts the fae held among the white birches, neither did he reject the noble honors bestowed upon him. But... what was he doing here?
...Until the moment of my departure, I received no clear answer to my inquiry, and his demeanor bore no resemblance to that of the calm and composed individual with whom I have long been familiar. It was as though all thoughts and sentiments within him dissolved into nothing but sighs of sorrow the moment he tried to utter them. Yet, by all I have seen and heard in the shadows these past days, I firmly believe that it was never his intention to conceal any of this from me... But no matter. The secrets buried here are as countless as the stars, and I fear this is but the most inconsequential among them...
...It is well that I possess ample time to seek out the truth in this long-forgotten homeland...

volumes.title: Notes by a Certain Noble Individual (II)
volumes.description: Notes by a Certain Noble Individual (II)
volumes.story:
...This is my eighth foray since I passed beyond that "curtain," and I have taken time to set down all observations from my investigations till now. Regrettably, as ever, I failed to obtain the answer I have been seeking...
...Once the patently fantastical accounts are set aside, the true history of Hyperborea appears to accord closely with the legends of the horned peoples of the south: that is, the city of usurpers was destroyed by the Celestial Nail sent down from above. Tales of this nature abound throughout Teyvat. I gravely doubt that the outcomes of these stories would have differed, even had the so-called angels lent their aid...
...In the records I have unearthed in the course of my search, an individual known as "The Saint" appears time and again. His true name, it would seem, was Anacharsis, and it was he who instigated the rebellion that courted eventual destruction...
...He was, in all likelihood, a prophet of some kind. The annals of mankind have never lacked figures of his ilk who, impelled by nothing but a fit of passion and unsubstantiated conviction, ultimately send countless others beyond the precipice of no return...
...To be so utterly consumed by folly and delusion appears innate to mankind — a failing that I, as one of the fae, have never understood. When I recall the motherland that should have endured to this day, and was instead reduced to its present state by this man's folly, my revulsion only intensifies...
...Yet ■■■■ admonishes me that it is ill-befitting to judge historical figures capriciously, and so I shall reserve further judgment until the facts of the matter are fully established. Furthermore, were that the sum of history, how would one explain my very existence? How came I to be born in a breeding ground, amidst the remains of a giant dragon, millennia after the motherland's annihilation? Why, too, did the "Great Judge" fail to purge the Shadow Realm — in which I now stand — the very moment it first emerged? All that I have witnessed here far surpasses any creation known to our age. Could such wonders truly have been wrought by the hands of man and angel?
...I have discussed these questions at great length with ■■■■, his reluctance notwithstanding. At the very least, he has elected not to drive me away, doubtless on account of all my efforts in restoring this castle...
...Meanwhile, the motives of the usurpers and the purpose of the Great Judge remain stubbornly resistant to all prying, much like these fog-shrouded ruins...
...I should go back now. It would seem that I am far better suited to a life spent riding in the wind, across the frozen wastes...

volumes.title: Notes by a Certain Noble Individual (III)
volumes.description: Notes by a Certain Noble Individual (III)
volumes.story:
...Foray number eighty-six: it is necessary that the many significant findings made over the last few years be recorded herewith...
...Through great effort, I have finally determined what transpired when the "passage" opened.
...The world of shadow may be likened to a film of oil resting upon the known world, and it is this film which separates Teyvat from the Abyss in the beyond. This film exists not merely on the spatial and material plane, but at the very intersections of the temporal and the spiritual. When I foolishly opened that passage, it was as though I had inflicted a great gash in time across the entire Shadow Realm, through which the Abyss now pours its filth into this world without end...
...But owing to the unique nature of the Shadow Realm, this corruption of our world has primarily manifested as a slow seepage. Though the process is irreversible, the threat remains manageable for the present...
...Might this stem from the fact that the Shadow Realm teems with possibilities yet unobserved? Should we follow this hypothesis, the relationship between the Shadow Realm and the Abyss may be one that is fundamentally antithetical and mutually repellent, explaining why the realm has remained untainted to this day...
...But wonderful though this possibility may seem, it is not without its price. Here, substance does not exist in a stable form — or rather, there is no true form, nor is any concretion possible. Yet whatever the truth may be, the science that brought the Shadow Realm into being lies beyond the grasp of even the sovereigns of this world. Undoubtedly, it is not a product of our world...
...The discoveries made thus far, however, complicate any explanation of why the Shadow Realm might have come to be... Could the protective or shielding effect the realm exerts upon our world be merely an outgrowth, an unintended consequence of the memories The Saint left behind in the eternal void in defiance of the fate the heavens had ordained for him?
...Why the Abyss continues to seep into this world remains obscure, though it is my firm belief that it bears some relation to the very purpose for which The Saint created the Shadow Realm...
...The above deductions were drawn from information I have gathered within the ruins. While many questions remain unresolved, the one thing we already know for certain is...
...We, the fae, were not born to be the servants of the humans of the golden realm as legend states. Those who have misrepresented us as slaves did so out of sheer fear of our existence amongst men. In fact, deep within these ruins that have since been covered by the sands, I have glimpsed that far more noble and grand ambition with which we were once entrusted...
...And in the oldest of these records, I have also since glimpsed the earliest name of the fae: Filii Adamici Evoluti, or "the evolved children of humanity."

volumes.title: Notes by a Certain Noble Individual (IV)
volumes.description: Notes by a Certain Noble Individual (IV)
volumes.story:
...Foray four hundred and forty-six: The records found alongside the Embryonic-Ichoric-Telluric-Rudiment, or "Eitr" for short, have provided a sufficiently clear picture of the matter, which is noted as follows...
...The Saint had come to Hyperborea in search of that light from the very genesis of the world, a fragment left behind at its inception. It is a light that is undissipated hope itself, a light that holds the potential to illuminate the entire cosmos. From what I have seen of it projected in that house of ministry, it is also the very same light that brought about my birth...
...He brought down something from the heavens merely to ascertain whether that light was truly extinguished. He then launched that advance which was destined to fail against the "fate" that ruled over the entire world, and was consequently punished...
...■■■■ was right. Hyperborea's fate had been sealed long before The Saint arrived. That long-written decree to annihilate the golden realm was one that even the eldest daughter of the angels could not alter, and all the men who remained faithful to the future could do was stave off the execution of that judgment for a mere thirty years. This fact alone is more than enough to disprove all of my earlier conclusions...
...As for the truth about "Heimarmene," I fear that the conclusion I have reached may be far too terrible to put to paper...
...That never-refracted light signified a boundless array of possibilities in its pure whiteness. However, man chose to confine it to a far narrower band of hues in the name of certainty, and so lost that very first shadow which the purest of light had cast into the void...
...Time moves in loops and circles. Therefore, whenever we lay down an anchor into fate, the Abyss will naturally lay an anchor into us at the end of time as well...
...I surmise this is something The Saint had long discerned. Perhaps he had even glimpsed that end of the path where the primordial first light had became spent, and thus resolved to cast himself headlong into the last light...
...Once we place this conclusion alongside the histories of the various nations, once seemingly unrelated events converge into a cohesive narrative. And even if memories cannot be retained in the Ley Lines, that will and desire to defy the heavens will nevertheless endure like twinkling stars through the few who survive and remain...
...Both the Goddess of Flowers in Sumeru and she who prophesied the rising of the waters in Fontaine sought to build systems that would stand independent of both the Ley Lines and Heimarmene. Though one may be unable to inflict substantial damage upon this severe and grinding world structure, a few rents and fissures suffice to loosen the threads of fate. And as the histories I have read attest, these defiers have indeed left their mark: in Natlan, the reins of power have been assumed by one other than a divinely anointed "Sacred Lord," whilst in Fontaine, the Remurians have somehow been able to elude the gaze of the high heavens and transmit their arts, albeit in a fashion distorted...
...Now, at last, I understand the great ambition once placed in my hands, and the responsibility I am meant to bear...
...The sin I have committed is utterly beyond forgiveness... I cannot deny my hand in that passage which traverses the Shadow Realm, nor that filth which continues to seep into the world. But there are other matters I must attend to before I atone for that sin. Or rather, only by attending to these matters can I redress the grave wrong I have committed...
....Only by ascending to that seat high up in the court of the stars and accomplishing that grand undertaking which our forebears could not achieve can the possibility of total destruction be averted...

volumes.title: Notes by a Certain Noble Individual (V)
volumes.description: Notes by a Certain Noble Individual (V)
volumes.story:
...My mind is made up. I shall accept the remains of the innocent, along with the throne promised by the heavens, if only to ensure that the sacrifices of the survivors and the forgotten shall never be in vain...
...In those days, neither The Saint nor the people of the golden realm knew that the will which once ruled the ancient universe had not yet been extinguished, and thus none could ascend the throne they had prepared. Yet, the spark they kindled has borne fruit thousands of years hence. That fruit was I — the posthumous child of that primordial first light...
...The throne bestowed by the heavens has proven to be far heavier than I had ever imagined, and it is only after claiming it that I finally understand that bitter expression on his face... When I first passed through the passage, ■■■■ could not reveal the secrets of ages past to me, for he bore the very same shackles that now bind me. Even so, I do not regret my decision, for this has always been my calling, the very purpose for which I was born upon this rock...
...The most glorious and the most base alike have been swept away, their memories erased by that Artificer who toys with living beings. In that eternal tyranny, history has been reduced to a blank slate time and again, until all progress, all that might be further built upon, and future itself have been rendered forever impossible...
...And so, to those who endure: never forget. Never forget either the great or the nameless, each of whom has offered up a sacrifice of their own. The "today" in which we now live shall one day become history, and when the future at last arrives, all shall be able , as I have, to look back upon the millennia of turmoil that came before and recount their tale. It is my hope that, when that day comes, none shall be forced to sift through dust and ruins in search of the faintest traces of the past, and that the names of those heroes shall instead live on in the songs of the people...
...as they sing in praise of that transcendence left unfulfilled, and of the dream in which so many had once placed their hopes...

volumes.story:
8: My notebook's missing. Did one of you take it?
25: Based on experience, it's more likely that you left it in a drawer somewhere.
8: I've looked. It's not in any of them.
45: But did you look in the dispensary?
65: If you still recall, you'd know that my dispensary may not be accessed by those younger than 18 years old.
25: What does this notebook look like?
8: It's a notebook with a black cover...
35: It's the kind they give out to all the Fatui.
25: Is there something important written in that notebook?
8: My experiment proposal's in there.
45: You're not planning on abducting Aranara for your experiment, are you? AHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!
65: What's so funny?
45: Don't you find this so adorable?
35: Seriously? Are you saying you're adorable?
Zandik: What's the matter with you? Why are you so quiet over there?
18: Well, the culprit has to keep a low profile, doesn't he? I'm the one who threw it out.
Zandik: ...
Zandik: Why did you do that?
18: Because it looked so childish.


25: Did all of you receive the notice about the Harbingers gathering?
65: What's the difference? If you received it, it means we all did too.
25: One of us has to sign on it to confirm receipt. Would you do it?
65: I'm not signing it.
25: Whoever signs it goes. I have a report to write.
Zandik: How about I just give you the day off? Since I'm the one you'll be handing that report to anyway.
25: No thanks!
35: It's done.
18: Are you really going?
8: Did you lose a bet or something?
35: Apparently we have a new colleague. I want to go check things out.
Zandik: I vaguely remember that I was maybe in my forties when I started becoming more of an introvert.
45: And we lost our sense of compassion at the age of eight.
35: It's not like I'm going to be compassionate towards a colleague anyway. I just want to get a feel for this new one.
25: I hope they're in HR.
18: I, for one, hope that they're in Finance.
35: What's with Pantalone?
18: He rejected my request.
8: Hehe...
45: Maybe it was just an administrative issue.


18: How was the party?
35: Meh. It's just some young girl transferred in from another branch.
18: Are you sure she's a young girl, or does she just look like one?
35: I'd never ask a question as rude as that. But based on my experience, it should be the latter.
18: That means... How old is the Tsaritsa now, anyway? I've never really kept track.
35: Do you know the answer? You tell him.
65: This is a total waste of time.
18: What? Can't I be curious?


45: "Madam Columbina"? "Miss Columbina"...?
65: Just call her by her name.
45: She feels so approachable for some reason, don't you think?
35: Just because she looks like she could do with a bit of care and concern?
45: And because she looks starving and miles away from everything that's going on.
18: Needless to say, none of that "everything" would be good news.
Zandik: She's the one the Tsaritsa has taken a liking to recently. And since she isn't actually involved in any of the Tsaritsa's "affairs," it implies that she's the "affair" itself.


8: A report from Sandrone just came in.
65: Leave it. I'll take a look at it later.
45: There's no real need to look at it anyway. Her theories are all so behind the times, and she's not exactly pioneering in her research ideas either.
35: If you ask me, she's actually more interesting than her science.
45: If you're talking about her personality, I suppose that's fair.
18: Who's on duty shift today? The equipment in the operating room was just replaced. I need your signature for the delivery.
45: This must be a gift from the equipment supplier. But why wasn't it mentioned in the letter?
18: I just saw it myself.
45: Yeah, the ones who need help are always the easiest to talk to. That's what I've always thought. Besides, I like how sincere she seems about wanting to work with us.
25: You're so cocky when you think you hold all the power. I'd love to see your face when it's your turn to put in a project funding request.
45: We have to have a united front on this. Dottore is supportive, but also letting things play out as they will.
65: That makes sense. Oh by the way, remember to attend that meeting called by Il Capitano tomorrow morning.
35: Right.


35: Which one of you was at the cafeteria earlier? Was it you?
25: How did you know?
35: I ran into The Rooster, and he said, didn't you just have your meal a few moments ago?
25: ...
35: The Jester might have noticed something wasn't quite right too. But he didn't say a thing.
25: Maybe because he was raised right?
35: Or maybe he was just unsure.
25: That's not surprising, I suppose. Who can really tell the whole lot of "me"s apart?
35: There's only one "me." Zandik's the main, and not a Segment.
25: The main doesn't count.
35: He doesn't count? Haha.
35: If you ask me, neither you nor me are truly "me"s.


45: The main just died, and the body is still fresh. I need all hands on deck! We need to prepare for the autopsy and start recording now.
25: Already recording. But do you have to be so excited?
65: In all honesty, our shared lack of imagination in these matters is almost impressive.
35: Do you actually not feel sorry for Zandik? You're the one who was closest to him.
65: Of course I feel sorry for Zandik. Am I not Zandik himself?
35: You're right, and I feel the same way. This is the time for us to show some emotion and compassion for ourself.
45: We should be able to develop a drug that works better on us since we're experimenting on our own body.
18: Let's get to it! I'm so excited!

volumes.story:
The plan has reached a critical stage. Daily security must be maintained without fail.
We've captured a rat attempting to infiltrate Izmaylov. By order of the Young Sire, security personnel and alert levels are to be reinforced.
The mechanisms in the Shadow Realm are reportedly in place... Refining Kresnik Kristall and completing the "Key" have become matters of utmost urgency.

That woman still refuses to talk. Who sent her? The "High Table"? Luchkin? Or the Energy Commission?

name: Yet-to-be-Completed "New High Table Rules"
description: A collection of literature preserved in the Royal Libraries of Teyvat.

volumes.title: Yet-to-be-Completed "New High Table Rules"
volumes.story:
The snow buries every story. Or perhaps it would be more fitting to say that the snow itself is an endless story.
Snow falls over Snezhnaya all year round. It buries everything, leaving behind nothing but a blank expanse. Yet beneath that snow lie bones and graves, lives that once burned with untamed vitality. They gave everything in the hope that someone would bear witness to them... Should they not be seen?
If I, Vasiliy, succeed, and you, as one of Izmaylov, live to witness this set of "New Rules" — then it will mean our great undertaking has taken its first step.
It will mean that I have secured for all at the "High Table" a place to stand as equals alongside those so-called "great figures."
I hope that when that day comes, none of you will have to remain hidden in the shadows any longer, living only as the foil to those who bask in the light. You will no longer have to bow and scrape or humble yourselves before others.
Instead, you will stand tall and proudly call yourselves "Izmaylov."
I long with all my heart for that future to come. And I, Vasiliy, will lead you there.

volumes.title: A "Letter" in a Diary
volumes.description: Vodyanitsa's Letter
volumes.story:
...You once told me I would understand someday, but even now, I still don't.
I don't believe anyone should be forced to abandon their homeland because of a change in power. She never considered the feelings of us Water Imp nobles.
Every inch of this land reflects memories of my childhood; if I close my eyes, I can still hear everyone's songs echoing everywhere. I will not forgive those who drove us away...
And I miss you very much, Mother.

volumes.title: A "Letter" in a Diary
volumes.description: Vodyanitsa's Letter
volumes.story:
I often find myself missing that dress with the tassels, the heavy bed curtains, and the first rays of sunlight that would stream into the manor each morning.
But it's alright now — if I narrow my eyes just a little, the light seeping through a crack backstage feels just like the one in our manor.
I know that life is gone forever, and I can miss it all I want, but I also feel that what I have here now is no less than what I lost.
The fantastical sets designed by the prop master, the many fans who come all this way just to see me, and the quiet dancing girl who doesn't talk much — these are all mine! I won't lose any of it again! Never! Absolutely never!

volumes.title: A "Letter" in a Diary
volumes.description: Vodyanitsa's Letter
volumes.story:
I've joined a rather remarkable organization, though I can't tell you its name, hehe.
Whatever that great figure intends to do this time, there should always be someone looking out for the misfortunes of ordinary people. That's what our organization exists for.
Even now, I still don't understand her. Why is it that those in power always seem this way? They clearly have the ability to bring greater happiness.
Some say she has her own difficulties. But what could possibly trouble someone so seemingly omnipotent?
Never mind. I should just focus on what I can do. I suppose you'll all hear about our organization sooner or later. Its name is... Ah, never mind. I'll leave it a mystery for now.

volumes.description: Report of Investigation Into Alleged Ghost Haunting
volumes.story:
...This commission is clearly not as simple as previous cases involving only "folklore studies." It appears to be connected to something far more mysterious.
An extinct civilization? The creations of ancient gods? Or powers from beyond this world? The possibilities leave ample room for speculation.
From now on, we should take this as a lesson: a simple surface does not imply that what lies beneath shares the same level of existence or nature.

volumes.title: Investigation Report into Supernatural Sightings at the Opera House
volumes.description: Report of Investigation Into Alleged Ghost Haunting
volumes.story:
Ley Lines themselves possess a powerful ability to either "devour" or "guide" souls. In most cases, once the soul and body of the deceased are separated, the soul is drawn directly into the Ley Lines, leaving no room for lingering existence.
However, evidence shows that the connection between the theater area and the Ley Lines has been obstructed, though only partially, not completely severed. Still, this has granted certain souls unwilling to return to the Ley Lines an opportunity: if their resistance is strong enough, they may even linger within the theater indefinitely.
In theory, however, these souls within the theater are incapable of influencing the physical world. Only under extremely rare circumstances can they produce phenomena observable to the human eye. Overall, they can be considered harmless. This assessment may be conveyed in advance to the theater's management to reassure them.

volumes.title: Investigation Report into Supernatural Sightings at the Opera House
volumes.description: Report of Investigation Into Alleged Ghost Haunting
volumes.story:
But for me, the investigation does not end here. Uncovering the reason why the Ley Lines have been obstructed is the true focus of this inquiry.
After consulting multiple sources, the most reliable hypothesis at present appears to be... "the existence of an angel civilization and its preliminary attempts at Ley Line renovation."
There is too little information available here. I must return home as soon as possible...

Okurov lies nestled within a valley, with a low-lying basin floor... Under the influence of ████, temperatures may rise and snowmelt may occur. If drainage within the valley proves insufficient, accumulated water could lead to severe flooding...
...
Thus, an underground channel system was constructed. First, for drainage. Second, for ████... From this, the tender sprout of ████ began to emerge. I have begun to discern the correct path forward...
...Must undergo three rounds of authentication... Obtain the <color=#00E1FFFF>Red, White, and Blue Keys</color>... placed at three different locations... Insert all three simultaneously into the slots to activate the gate...
...
Inserting either the <color=#00E1FFFF>White or Blue Key</color> into the control console will lower the water level. Inserting both the <color=#00E1FFFF>White and Blue Key Cards</color> will fully drain it...
...
...The locations of the <color=#00E1FFFF>Red, White, and Blue Keys</color> are shown above.
For me, who may one day return to this place... When the floodwaters of melted snow become nourishment for life... when useless memories fade into indistinct echoes of the past... when I make my way to ████ one day...

<title name = Exciting New Astronomical Discovery! Mystery Creature Found on the Moon?/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_01/>
<center>Exciting New Astronomical Discovery! Mystery Creature Found on the Moon?</center>
Our newspaper learned yesterday from an observatory in the Far North — the location of which, owing to the confidential nature of unpublished research, cannot presently be revealed — that the eminent astronomer Dr. Ivan Hershelev has, with the aid of his newly invented giant microscopic telescope, at last succeeded in observing the magnificent spectacle that is the surface of the moon.
The principle underlying this novel giant microscopic telescope sprang from a stroke of genius on the part of Dr. Hershelev. By mounting a compound microscope of no fewer than 24-fold magnifying power upon the eyepiece of a gigantic telescope measuring upwards of 70 feet in length, he has achieved nothing less than a revolutionary triumph over the established limits of optical science. With the supplementation of intense illumination produced by highly refined Kresnik Kristall, this new invention certainly has achieved an unprecedented degree of magnification.
It has also come to light that the source of funding for this extraordinary enterprise was the Armory Palace, though until now the project had never been disclosed to the public, nor had it appeared in any annual statement of expenditures. When queried on this matter, Dr. Hershelev stated that, all parties concerned had long since been enjoined to observe the strictest secrecy in order to secure for the Fatui an undisputed supremacy in the scientific competition among the various nations. This is perhaps the reason that we have only learned today of this pioneering undertaking, an enterprise daring to pierce the very veil of the cosmos.
In a letter which Dr. Hershelev has entrusted to this paper for publication, he describes in great detail the wondrous scenery observed upon the surface of the moon — including its forests, its rivers, its valleys, and boundless grasslands — as well as the host of marvelous creatures inhabiting that realm: bison, whales, jellyfish... and even penguins!
Dr. Hershelev also draws particular attention to what he believes to be evidence of an intelligent race upon the moon: a magnificent palace built entirely out of blue crystal, with lofty towers that stand pointed directly toward our own world! What message, one cannot help but wonder, do its builders seek to convey? Might this be a triumphant proclamation of their civilization's glory and superiority? Or could it be a stark warning of the calamities that await our own?
In the closing of his letter, Dr. Hershelev relates yet another extraordinary discovery. According to him, a humanoid creature of uncertain nature, adorned with golden fur and bearing a pair of delicate membranous wings upon its back, was observed wandering repeatedly through the telescope's field of view. Unfortunately, before its likeness could be committed to photographic image, the observation was brought to an abrupt end. Dr. Hershelev had, it turned out, neglected to lower and secure the telescope before retiring for the night. Then, at sunrise, the rays of the sun, passing through the instrument and concentrated by its lenses, ignited a fire. But thankfully, the staff members present acted with admirable promptness, and the flames were extinguished before any loss of life or injury could occur.
Though this remarkable undertaking was brought to an untimely close by the accident, the advancements that have been made so far are enough to shake up the scientific world. Predictably, certain hidebound individuals of the academy have denounced the entire enterprise as "pure invention," Yet scholars of the Rtawahist school at the Akademiya have responded to Dr. Hershelev's work with the utmost enthusiasm. So astonishing were the disclosures contained in his letter, several Herbad are said to have swooned on the spot upon reading them.
In the six issues to follow, this paper will have the honor of presenting, in full, the remarkable letter entrusted to us by Dr. Hershelev. Readers eager to uncover the truth of the moon will not wish to miss a single installment!

<title name = Tales of the Strange and Incredible: The Volkodlak Miners Who Rode the Train No More (Contributor Story)/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_09/>
<center>Tales of the Strange and Incredible: The Volkodlak Miners Who Rode the Train No More (Contributor Story)</center>
Contributor: Mr. Mamontov

This is a story told to me by way of a friend of a friend.

Lishin had been with the Transport Bureau for less than a year. Born in Svetloledovka, his greatest ambition had always been to leave his hometown and make a life for himself in one of the great cities like Snezhnograd or Novokitezhgrad. That ambition had now been fulfilled, if only in part. As a railway attendant, he had been assigned to the very line connecting Svetloledovka with Novokitezhgrad and Snezhnograd alike.
Blessed with an easy manner and a gift for conversation, Lishin soon grew familiar with the regular passengers on his route. Their idle chatter provided no shortage of tales: the particulars of a Chicota investigation, a Snegovik's account of the House of Hesperides, and the like. Such stories lent him a certain worldly air whenever he returned to Svetloledovka and traded reminiscences with old friends who had never left home. He came to genuinely enjoy the work, whatever his original motives may have been, until the incident that left him gravely ill.

That day had begun as an altogether ordinary day for Lishin. In the car were a few students returning to their studies, a young couple animatedly discussing the season's newest stage production, a tall and melancholic Snegovik, several Volkodlak miners... Many of them were faces that had long become familiar to him.
The Volkodlak miners, in particular, were in rather high spirits. According to them, something had been unearthed far west of Novokitezhgrad. It was something, they insisted, that ought not to be spoken of openly. Yet, they could not resist sharing the news with their fellow passengers, as extraordinary as said discovery was. Having overheard them, the melancholic Snegovik offered a warning: "If what was taken came from the ruins of Kitezhgrad, you would do well to return it without delay. Otherwise, misfortune will follow."
A chill ran down Lishin's spine at these words. It was almost as though the warning had taken effect the very instant it was uttered. He inspected the train's heating apparatus and found it in perfect working order, yet that peculiar chill seemed to linger throughout the car all the same. Should he report the matter, and have the detectives called in to investigate? Though he wished to be a conscientious and diligent member of the staff, he had no desire to earn the contempt reserved for informers.

But the dilemma did not trouble him for long, for that very evening he was struck by a severe fever. This was most unusual for a man who had always enjoyed robust health. The unexplained illness forced him to take a week's leave of absence, and even after returning to work, he found himself afflicted with a lingering weakness, his constitution far diminished from what it had once been.
According to one of Lishin's colleagues at the Transport Bureau, the other passengers aboard the train that day had also fallen ill at almost precisely the same time, and some of those in weaker health had yet to recover even to this day. This same colleague even took the trouble to consult a relative in Novokitezhgrad who had the gift of communicating with the unseen world, and the answer he received was: the Volkodlak miners had carried some unclean thing aboard the train and incurred the curse of Chernabog. Their fellow passengers, and Lishin himself, fell ill from being possessed by wicked spirits. When told of this, though Lishin was ready to dismiss the claim outright, the memory of that strange chill creeping upward from beneath his feet like a serpent gave him pause.

Lishin never saw or heard of those Volkodlak miners again. Perhaps it was simply a matter of their work, and they no longer had cause to travel on that particular route. Or perhaps Chernabog, angered by their actions, had... Whatever the truth may have been, it was as if their figures, or perhaps their very existence, had been erased by the endless winds and snows of the tundra, with not even the slightest trace left behind.

This has, in turn, caused countless passengers to suffer severe chills and illness.
The Bureau also stressed that, while Mr. Ivanov himself had acted without malice, it had nevertheless been compelled to prohibit him from boarding its trains to safeguard the health and safety of other passengers, and sought the public's understanding on this matter.

<center>Tales of the Strange and Incredible: Through Stars and Nightmares - Mr. Feodor's Time-Space-Defying Journey (Contributor Story)</center>
Word has reached us regarding a certain Mr. Feodor, a naturalist currently under retainer with the Adventurers' Guild. Though remarkably quiet and rather hopeless at small talk, he enjoys high esteem among his peers for his vast erudition and razor-sharp intellect. Even the Guild's most seasoned adventurers routinely find themselves humbled by his seemingly endless store of knowledge.
Yet, as only his dear wife knows, this seemingly omniscient expert was a jobless, heavy-drinking, middle-aged mess a mere five years ago. Quite what caused such a dramatic overnight transformation remains a total mystery to her, but she is utterly thrilled all the same, if only because it spares her from worrying herself sick day in and day out!
Then, on a summer day this past year, Mr. Feodor collapsed mid-lecture right in front of his eager adventurer pupils. Upon waking, he could no longer answer a single scholarly question and even claimed to have no recollection whatsoever of ever being a naturalist.
According to him, he had just spent five years trapped in an interminable nightmare. He claimed that a race of star-faring beings known as the "Chroniclers" had whisked his soul away to countless strange worlds, then eventually dropped him off in a Teyvat ruled by reptiles and lizards. It was only then that he realized he had landed in a primordial age unrecorded by history. Then, prompted by these strange folk, he duly jotted down a full five-year chronicle of his wild travels, then left the manuscript behind in a castle of lizards.
Shortly after, poor Mr. Feodor was packed off to a sanitarium for treatment. The good doctors there insisted he was merely suffering from a nervous affliction, and in time, the gentleman came around to their view, convincing himself that the entire affair was nothing more than a bad dream.
Yet just last month, a top-secret letter arrived from a band of adventurers who had once studied under Mr. Feodor. Deep within a ruin in Natlan, these daring fellows actually dug up the ancient manuscript he had once insisted he had authored... written, just as he described, from stone tablets of a peculiar kind.
And so our strange little tale draws to a close here. While Mr. Feodor's nightmare may never truly end, it leaves us with a far more chilling question: as you lay down in bed tonight, can you be entirely certain that the person sleeping beside you is still the very soul you remember?

The authors of the study note that hot baths raise body temperature. As a result, the pores of the skin open, allowing harmful substances in the air that cause various ailments to enter the body. At the same time, hot baths also damage the skin's natural protective layer of microorganisms, thereby weakening immunity.

<title name = Tales of the Strange and Incredible: The Headless Train Attendant in the Snow (Contributor Story)/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_05/>
<center>Tales of the Strange and Incredible: The Headless Train Attendant in the Snow (Contributor Story)</center>
Contributor: Mr. Mamontov

This is a story told to me by way of a friend of a friend.

Andrei had never in his wildest dreams imagined that he should one day be reduced to such a state: penniless, and tending the locomotive's firebox for no other reason than to scratch out a living and repay his debt to the gang, one small installment at a time. Once, he had a respectable business in Novokitezhgrad. But by this point, his shop had been seized, his fiancée had, quite naturally, released him from their engagement, and even his own family had refused him assistance, turning him out of their home.

The source of all his misfortunes lay in a certain game he should have never even dipped his toes in. At first, he genuinely believed that fortune had smiled upon him, and that the card table would fill his purse beyond measure. Little did he understand that winning is always fleeting, while loss is the one true constant.
His last hopes had lain with an old friend of his, Zharanov, who had whispered of a secret hidden somewhere in Nod-Krai — a secret, he claimed, that would be more than enough to clear the debts they both owed, if only Andrei would see fit to invest in the venture and finally take it off the ground. But when Zharanov left and never returned, and nothing more was heard of him, Andrei's last hope vanished as well.
The wages of a locomotive stoker would certainly have never interested him before. But now, they were all he had. At such a rate, when would he ever repay his debt and see daylight again? Maybe it was better that he kept the money and tried his luck once more at the card table with it. Better that than throw the cash to the gang, and into a bottomless pit... Surely the gang would not do anything too drastic over a few missed payments. Yet whenever the thought came to mind, the memory of losing everything would make him shrink back. And so the days wore on, consumed by hesitation and torment, and punctuated only by the sounds of the train whistle.

Then, one night, as the train labored through a raging blizzard, its headlights carving a narrow path through the darkness and driving snow, something appeared without warning in that narrow corridor of light. It was a ragged man, carrying a lantern, staggering alongside the tracks like a ghost.
It was a day so awfully cold, one could hardly breathe. No ordinary person apart from the fae could have endured more than half an hour in such weather. Moved by instinctive pity, Andrei was about to ask the conductor to slow the train when he found the latter staring out the window, his face drained of all color. Following his gaze, Andrei saw what he had not noticed before: the figure struggling through the snow had nothing upon its shoulders. Where its head should have been, there only burned a cold, unnatural flame.
The train chugged on, with no sign of slowing. As though fearful of disturbing the headless wanderer, it gave no whistle, but merely passed him by, leaving that solitary flame behind in the boundless night.

It was only after they had passed that shocking sight that the conductor, still shaken, began to tell him an old story long since forgotten...
It was a story about a man named Old Kashchin who used to work on the line. He was not a bad sort, apart from the fact that he was an inveterate drunkard and had no sense for money. Everyone knew he owed the gang a debt he would never repay, but he never seemed troubled by it. As long as they still expected him to work it off, they could hardly kill him... or so he reckoned. And in the end, everyone left him be.
Then came the night the train ran through this desolate section of track. A passenger reported strange noises from the roof, suspecting damage left behind by Vila raiders. Old Kashchin's supervisor sent Kashchin up for a check despite the latter's misgivings.

No one ever learned what he saw up there. All anyone heard was a heavy thud from the roof, and then Old Kashchin's head, his face still frozen in surprise, rolled past the car windows and into the snow, where the darkness and the blizzard swallowed it swiftly.
It was no ordinary attack, but an execution. Two men from the gang had run a line, fine as a thread yet impossibly strong, across the track, and when Old Kashchin climbed onto the roof, it took his head clean off.

"This is what he owed the Izmaylovs,"
Said the two bandits who rapped on the train window, then flew away.

From that day on, Old Kashchin became a prisoner of the line, finding no rest and condemned to wander out in the snow with his battered lantern. He was doomed to forever search for the debt he could never repay... and for the head he had lost.

<title name = Snowland Sensations: The Myth of Al-Ahmar, the False King (Contributor Story)/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_09/>
<center>Snowland Sensations: The Myth of Al-Ahmar, the False King (Contributor Story)</center>
New Teyvat Chronicles: Sumeru (III)
The Fiction That is the "History of the Desert": We Begin With Al-Ahmar

In earlier installments of this serial, we have put forward a startling premise: Decarabian, Al-Ahmar, Remus, and Och-Kan — these so-called rulers were never real historical figures at all. Rather, they are merely regional variations of a single, shared historical prototype: Tsar Monomakh.

With just a bit of digging, it becomes glaringly obvious that these fictitious rulers all share the same telltale characteristics:

First, they were all branded by later historians as "tyrants" (because they refuse to admit that Tsar Monomakh once conquered and ruled the entire world);

Second, no physical remains are in evidence (because Tsar Monomakh lies at rest at Pale Crown Palace, a fact they simply cannot alter);

And third, the so-called "historical ruins" associated with them are all later fabrications (all because their own civilized history is so brief, forcing them to invent a fake past).

Take, for instance, the history of the Sumeru desert so blindly trusted by mainstream academia: it is riddled with glaring holes that fail to hold up under scrutiny:

First of all, what did they eat?

As we all know, the Deserts of Sumeru are, quite literally, deserts. Forget thousands of years ago; even today, a desert could never sustain such a vast population. So how could anyone have possibly built the magnificent Mausoleum of King Deshret?

Second: How was The Mausoleum of King Deshret maintained through the ages?

Granted, while the author has never visited Sumeru in person, the desert region conspicuously lacks any trace of large-scale quarries. Furthermore, no known form of transport could have ever moved such immense quantities of stone over such vast distances.

This is where the truth practically leaps off the page: the so-called "Mausoleum of King Deshret" was in fact built by Tsar Monomakh himself, and the name we know of today simply came from a mispronunciation by later desert dwellers. First, they inverted "mono" and "makh" into "Makh-mono." Then, due to oral transmission, they weakened the initial consonant (a common enough occurrence across languages), and the name underwent a slight vowel shift into "Akh-mana," and ultimately corrupted it into today's "Al-Ahmar."

While in Nod-Krai, the author had the good fortune of meeting a young lady from the Sumeru desert, who sold me a set of amulets reputedly forged by Al-Ahmar himself. Upon closer inspection, it was discovered that these very amulets were inscribed in Fontainian script with the words "For use at the Fontinalia Film Festival." Naturally, a lady of such beauty and elegance would never lie. This leaves us with only one possible conclusion: the entire history of Sumeru was, in fact, fabricated by Fontaine!

Furthermore, the lady offered another piece of crucial supporting evidence: she revealed that her people all refer to Al-Ahmar as the "God of Love." But as we all know, in that era, only one figure was ever hailed as the God of Benevolence: Tsar Monomakh himself...

<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_05/>
<center>Tales of the Strange and Incredible: Horror in the Hills (Contributor Story)</center>
Whether man or fae, people today instinctively cling to the belief that the world operates on a set of benevolent — or at the least, intelligible — rules. Yet, because our minds and intellects are but products of this world, from the perspective of logic and mathematics we can never truly apprehend the world's reality in full.

For us, this may well be the greatest mercy the world bestows. Once, I had a glimpse (may Her Majesty preserve my soul) of things so profane and abhorrent, no human should ever comprehend them. Words fail to capture what I witnessed, and no known language can articulate that primordial, maddening horror. I once swore that as long as I lived, I would never speak of what A. G. Pamiyev and I endured. I kept my silence, for people would have deemed me insane otherwise. Yet Mr. Pamiyev is now dead, and I shall soon follow him into the dark. Thus, I am compelled to publish the report that was withheld back then, if only to rest in peace in the thereafter. Should death erase my memories entirely, it will be a true blessing.

The report is as follows:

Horror in the Hills? Newlyweds Meet Mysterious End in Svetloledovka

The Royal Railway Transport Bureau of Snezhnaya recently uncovered the bodies of two young persons, who had been missing for days, just outside the estate of Viscount A. Pamiyev.

Reports confirm the pair were a newlywed couple (names withheld by request) who had ventured into the mountains for their honeymoon, only to meet a tragic end on territory held for generations by Snegovik nobility. Even veteran officers long accustomed to seeing the dead were left shaken to their core by the sheer horror of the scene.

In an interview, Viscount Pamiyev pointed to three major mysteries about the case that remain completely unresolved:

First: Footprints in the snow indicate a desperate flight for survival in the couple's final moments. Not only had their tent been shredded from the inside, they had also cast aside their heavy winter boots for some reason. With massive strides, they had sprinted wildly through the deep snow, as if fleeing some unimaginable terror. Yet across the vast, empty expanse, no other tracks existed besides their own frantic, bare footprints.

Second: In stark contrast to the various signs of a frenetic final flight, the deceased bore no trace of agony or terror on their faces. Instead, their features were frozen in a state of what can only be called profound peace, complete with smiles of unsettling, almost eerie satisfaction.

Third: Among the victims' belongings, police recovered a Kamera containing just one photograph, heavily blurred and flooded with an eerie halo of light.

Watch this space for further developments on this chilling case.

...

That was all to that account. The writer had omitted the obscure, nearly forgotten stories surrounding the Pamiyev bloodline. One chronicle, allegedly compiled during the 53rd fae era, claimed that the Pamiyevs were "cursed by a god," though the deity in question was certainly not the Tsar Monomakh. Most of these rumors were chilling, cryptic tales suggesting that a sinister, profane cult operated within the family. These tales were so horrifying, they made the infamous nobles of Fontaine and Mondstadt seem as pure as ascetics by comparison.

I first met Andrei Grigorovich Pamiyev five years ago. Back then, I too believed these stories were nothing more than crude superstitions...

<center>Hero at the Helm — or a Shocking Secret? Exclusive Train Derailment Investigation!</center>
Freight train I-330 recently derailed while traveling from Snezhnograd to Novokitezhgrad. Despite the accident, no casualties were reported.

According to initial reports, the conductor on duty — identified here by the pseudonym Mr. Turkin — resorted to a series of unusually aggressive emergency measures. His actions ultimately enabled all passengers and crew to escape unharmed. What was initially hailed, and widely followed, as an "emergency rescue," however, has since come under closer scrutiny. With preliminary investigative procedures now underway, specific aspects of the operation are being formally reviewed, and questions have been raised over accountability for some of the measures taken.

The preliminary accident report focuses on a split-second decision that ran counter to standard safety protocol. Mr. Turkin claimed that, on the day of the incident, he saw a landslide suddenly develop directly in the train's path. Believing that conventional emergency braking could not bring the train to a halt within the remaining distance, he instead chose to break up the consist. The fully loaded freight cars at the rear were forcibly uncoupled and left behind. With only the locomotive and personnel carriages remaining, Mr. Turkin accelerated through the landslide zone.

The personnel carriages ultimately cleared the affected area, with only minor abrasions reported among some passengers. The abandoned freight cars, however, were completely buried, along with the substantial volume of state supplies they had been carrying. The full extent of the resulting property loss remains difficult to determine.

The Railway Transport Bureau has since opened a formal post-incident review and accountability process. At the center of the inquiry is evidence that may call Mr. Turkin's account into question. A technical specialist involved in the preliminary assessment, speaking to this newspaper on condition of anonymity, said the line's warning systems had issued the hazard alert in advance and in accordance with established procedure. "Under the standard emergency response plan, the conductor should have applied the emergency brakes the moment the alert was received," the specialist said. "Uncoupling and abandoning the freight cars without authorization was a serious violation, as was accelerating through the disaster zone with the personnel carriages in tow. Both actions breached the Standard Operating Procedures for Rail Transport Safety."

The accident commission's final report must now determine whether Mr. Turkin's actions constituted a justified response to an extreme emergency — or a serious overreaction arising from a flawed assessment of the danger. It must also establish whether the valuable supplies left behind were truly beyond saving. Until those findings are released, the line between heroism and misconduct remains unresolved. This newspaper will continue to follow the investigation.

The Seven Impossible Mysteries of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire: The Platinum Piece
Chapter V

...

"Indeed, you are entirely correct," Grand Duke Brahe Trubetskoy replied with serene composure. "Your poor wife has always been thus — forever yearning after a life of unbounded luxury, and resolved to live, and spend, with all the prodigality of a true grand duchess."

"So... am I to understand, Your Excellency, that my wife stole your platinum chess piece?" The color fled Viscount Shuisky's face, leaving it as white as the snow beyond the windows. Almost at once, however, his complexion darkened to a livid grey. The inference was so preposterous, and the shock of it so profound, that he appeared scarcely able to comprehend what he had heard. "No, no... How could she possibly have done such a thing?"

"Vanity is her great weakness," the Grand Duke continued at his leisure. "But you, Andrei Dmitriyevich, possess only the rank and revenues of a viscount. You might have ground every unfortunate soul upon your estates beneath the millstone, pressing them like Rimecurrants until not a drop of oil remained to be wrung from them, and still her insatiable vanity would have demanded more. And thus resentment began to put forth its first shoots within your heart, rank as brambles and thornweed. That, however, was only part of the matter. Your noble and kindly heart had found another object for its affections: Miss Milady de Este, the celebrated Fontainian diva lately arrived from the Opera Epiclese. Is it not so? Oh, pray do not misunderstand me. I have no wish to reproach you for loving her. Indeed, what man could behold so pampered and imperious a beauty — so dazzling in her ostentation, like a peacock in full display — and not feel his heart stirred? No, it was not your love that condemned you, but what you did in its name. For her sake, you murdered your wife. You appropriated the treasure I had entrusted to your keeping, a precious relic bestowed upon me by His late Imperial Majesty. And, most contemptible of all, you fastened the sordid charge of absconding with the valuables upon your poor dead wife, knowing that she could no longer utter a word in her own defense. Ah, even one dog would not treat another so! And your wife was so beautiful... and loved you so dearly."

The Viscount kept his eyes fixed upon the Grand Duke's almost preternaturally handsome face. Meanwhile, as though guided by an impulse of which he was scarcely conscious, his right hand slipped deep into the pocket of his overcoat. His cracked lips quivered. He seemed on the verge of speaking, yet no sound emerged. He merely opened and closed his mouth like a fish cast upon the shore. At length, he lurched to his feet. A look of sorrow, almost of self-pity, had settled over his features, and when at last he found his voice, it came harsh and hoarse.

"My good man, my dear Brahe Prokhorovitch, what extraordinary notion is this? I beg you, hear me before you proceed any further... From whose contemptible lips did you receive so baseless a calumny, conceived in malice and fashioned wholly from lies? And why should you — a man whom I have always esteemed as good — choose to inflict such torment upon a bereaved husband, accusing him, His Majesty preserve us, of having murdered the wife dearest to his heart? You must pardon the liberty, Brahe Prokhorovitch, but are you fully master of your reason? It is beyond comprehension, beyond all comprehension... You would impute so monstrous a deed to me? To me, Andrei Dmitriyevich Shuisky, a gentleman upon whom His Majesty himself conferred the dignity of a title? How deeply you have wounded me! Yet the respect due to your exalted station compels me to say it once more: I have done nothing wicked, nothing contrary to heaven or conscience. As for this accusation that I appropriated the platinum chess piece, it is an injustice beyond measure, sheer nonsense from beginning to end. Perhaps you have drunk rather too much hot tea. Perhaps some delirium has seized you... But no matter. Have it as you will! Send men to search my residence this very instant. Let them prise up every floorboard and strip the plaster from every wall. If you find so much as—"

"Then be so good as to remove your glove. The one upon your right hand, if memory serves."

...

<title name = Now Hiring: Private Security Guards — Generous Pay!/>

<center>Hiring Private Guard for Top Pay</center>
HIRING URGENTLY! TOP PAY!

I, Grand Duke Diomid Turzov, seek to employ private guards and am prepared to offer generous compensation to suitable candidates.
(The sentence above was the best my servant could write. I fired him as soon as he finished it. He had no culture, no sense, and was very, very stupid. So I'm writing the rest myself. Everything below was written by me, Grand Duke Turzov, your favorite Grand Duke.)

I built a fountain. It is enormous. Without question, it is the most beautiful fountain in all of Snezhnaya. Maybe even the most beautiful in all of Teyvat. Better than the Fountain of Lucine. Much better. Everyone's talking about it. Then some horrible Tidalga got into the fountain. From Fontaine! They made the water look ugly. Total disaster. Very sad. But I fixed it. I did what no one else was brave enough to do! I drained the fountain and painted the bottom with beautiful, bright paint. After that, it looked incredible. So incredible!

Then the idiots on the Snezhnograd Veche ruined everything. There is something very wrong with their brains, by the way. They knew the paint would feed the Tidalga, but did they tell me? No. Of course not. Soon there were more Tidalga than ever! Total disaster! But I fixed that too. I always do. I poured a huge amount of bleach into the fountain, and it became clean again. I won. A historic victory, like no one's ever seen!

But the thugs from the Rokot are still not giving up. They want to destroy everything. My big, beautiful paint has started peeling. My servants say the bleach caused it, but that is obviously fake news. Totally fake. The truth is simple! Those losers are sneaking into the manor at night and tearing the paint off with their filthy hands! Embarrassing. So embarrassing!

These paint-scraping lunatics will be found, and we're gonna lock them up! To make sure of that, I am going to spend a great, super great deal of money hiring the biggest, toughest, strongest warriors money can buy. A very, very great deal of money. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

<title name = Theft Denied, Murder Admitted? An Ongoing Investigation into the Missing "Star of the Snowfield"/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_04/>
<center>Theft Denied, Murder Admitted? An Ongoing Investigation into the Missing "Star of the Snowfield"</center>
This paper reports:

The Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau has announced the arrest of a suspect in the long-running investigation into the disappearance of the "Star of the Snowfield."

According to Officer Yudintsev, who conducted the interrogation, the suspect — identified here by the pseudonym V. Buyanov — entered the victim's residence in the early hours of the morning. He is alleged to have stolen the priceless jewel known as the "Star of the Snowfield" and murdered the victim, identified here by the pseudonym A. Valannikov.

During interrogation, Buyanov firmly denied stealing the jewel, but readily confessed to the killing.

"Yes, I killed Valannikov (pseudonym). He was a swindler and a loan shark. But I did not steal from him. That is not why I turned myself in. I came forward because I believed I had killed something greater than a man — though, apparently, I did not even manage the killing very well. What I killed was a principle. A principle! Do you understand? I confessed to the murder of my own free will, and yet you insist on accusing me of taking some ridiculous possession. You are a good man, but I will not accept that accusation."

Valannikov's (pseudonym) lady companion, however, rejected Buyanov's denial in heated terms:

"...If that murderer did not steal the 'Star of the Snowfield,' then who did? Never mind my poor Valannikov (pseudonym) for one moment — who else could possibly have taken it? In Her Majesty's name, send the man to the gallows at once! As for the jewel, simply record it as lost. There is no need to waste any more time searching for it... What I mean is, we should be thinking about Valannikov's (pseudonym) funeral, should we not? The murderer is already in custody. Compared with that, what importance could one or two missing jewels possibly have?"

Further updates will follow as the case develops.

<title name = A Triumph for Security in the Capital! "Wandering Samurai" Who Terrorized Citizens for Weeks Brought to Justice!/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_02/>
<center>A Triumph for Security in the Capital! "Wandering Samurai" Who Terrorized Citizens for Weeks Brought to Justice!</center>
Exclusive Report: The shadow over Snezhnograd has finally lifted. The Inazuman "Wandering Samurai," whose violent rampage kept the capital in fear for weeks, was captured in a pre-dawn operation yesterday.
For weeks, a masked Kairagi had been striking late at night across Snezhnograd's Downtown District and along secluded paths beyond Glupov, leaving the city increasingly fearful as the number of victims grew. Eyewitnesses described him as wearing battered crimson armor and a bizarre mask. Combined with his uncanny swordsmanship, his frightening appearance was reportedly enough to make several victims drop their belongings and flee before he could say a word.
Following a coordinated investigation led by the Criminal Investigation Division and Druzhna patrol units under the personal supervision of Snezhnograd's Police Chief, the culprit was successfully apprehended late last night. The investigation proceeded without interruption, with officers working day and night until the suspect was located inside an abandoned bakery in the Downtown District. When the fully armed culprit attempted to leave the premises to commit another crime, the patrol teams stationed nearby immediately took action and subdued him!
Investigations reveal that the criminal was a licensed merchant from Ritou in Inazuma. Due to an irreconcilable conflict of interest between the mercantile association and the Kanjou Commission in charge of the area at the time, said association was rendered bankrupt two years ago. Unwilling to revert to being a common citizen, the criminal, backed into a corner, stole crimson armor and a sacred blade that had been offered to a local shrine, then fled the country. First, the criminal fled to the border region of Nod-Krai and engaged in rank charlatanry by assuming the status of an Inazuman Samurai. After being exposed by the Curatorium of Secrets, he then sneaked into Her Majesty's sacred capital, Snezhnograd, planning to continue his deceptions. However, after discovering that he could plunder at will by relying on his terrifying attire, the offender repeatedly employed the same tactic. He was eventually apprehended by law enforcement after inciting city-wide panic.
As the criminal is a fugitive, the Inazuman authorities have refused to recognize his expatriate status. As such, he now awaits judgment under Snezhnayan law. For further updates on how this case shall progress, please keep an eye out for the latest news.

<title name = Tales of the Strange and Incredible: The Jack Frost Witch (Contributor Story)/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_09/>
<center>Tales of the Strange and Incredible: The Jack Frost Witch (Contributor Story)</center>
Contributor: Shagova (pseudonym)

I'm Shagova, an adventurer. A few days ago, I accepted a commission and set out for one of the most dangerous snowfields on the outskirts of Snezhnaya. (And yes, I went alone. Before you ask why I would venture into such a perilous place without anyone by my side, the answer is simple: I wanted the entire reward for myself! Besides, I'm a highly capable adventurer!)

Unfortunately, all my preparations proved useless when a sudden blizzard swept in and left me hopelessly lost in the snowfield. The cold was unbearable, and before long, I felt as though I might freeze to death. With no other options left, I remembered a story my grandmother had told me long ago:

"Child, listen carefully... If you ever find yourself lost in a vast, endless snowfield, recite that ancient incantation, and the Jack Frost Witch will appear from the depths of the storm. But remember, only when you are trapped in the darkest and most hopeless of situations may you call upon her name..."

It took me quite some time, but eventually, I managed to dig the incantation out from the depths of my childhood memories: "Haskratol-rabkadisumavits-kuporomgozinadek." (And believe me, I know how it sounds, but I wasn't simply making those words up! I have my own brain to thank for remembering such a tremendous amount of completely useless information!)

As it turned out, my grandmother's story was true after all. The Jack Frost Witch appeared before me, soaring through the storm on her broom, with a group of round and plump Jack Frosts trailing behind her. She rescued me from the snowfield and brought me back to her courtyard. Yet my troubles were far from over. The witch told me that she would send me home if I fulfilled her wish. But if I failed, she would turn me into flower fertilizer.

So, what exactly did the Jack Frost Witch want from me? A choir. More specifically, a Jack Frost choir. The problem was that the Jack Frosts had absolutely no interest in cooperating, and every attempt at singing together ended in complete chaos. Yet somehow, I was expected to turn them into a well-trained choir capable of singing together perfectly by the following morning.

Don't ask me how I managed it. All I can say is that I'm very grateful I wasn't turned into flower fertilizer.
(Unfortunately, despite making it deep into the snowfield, I still failed to complete my client's commission. My reward... gone...)

Still, I wanted to share this spell for summoning the Jack Frosts with everyone. Perhaps it may save your life someday!

"Haskratol-rabkadisumavits-kuporomgozinadek!"

Though, I should warn you, it may also result in you becoming flower fertilizer. On the bright side, you might just be lucky enough to hear a well-trained Jack Frost choir perform a beautiful harmony together!

<title name = Grand Exhibition of Prime Ice Sculptures to Be Held in Snezhnograd/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_03/>
<center>Grand Exhibition of Prime Ice Sculptures to Be Held in Snezhnograd</center>
A grand exhibition of Prime Ice sculpture art will soon open in Snezhnograd. Organized with the Snezhnograd Veche's continued dedication to enriching the cultural lives of the people and guided by its careful deliberation, the event will feature the special exhibition "Classics, Redux: The Glaciafruit Master Returns (A Special Homage Exhibition)." Jointly arranged by the Veche and the Prime Ice Art Alliance, the exhibition offers citizens and all admirers of Snezhnayan culture an opportunity to witness the artistry of a master and gain a deeper understanding of the nation's cultural traditions.

More than a rare artistic occasion — one that comes only once in a decade — the exhibition also marks an important milestone in bringing Prime Ice art closer to the people. According to Ms. Kustodiev, Acting Chairwoman of the Prime Ice Art Alliance, the history of this art form has long been defined by its immense cost: "For many years, the creation of Prime Ice sculptures remained an art reserved exclusively for the court. During the era of the Pale Star Court, a poem recorded the reality of those times: 'To the halls of nobles were delivered countless Prime Ice sculptures; yet the miners of Zolnyy could not claim even a bowl of red Borsch.' Those words remain a true reflection of history."

Ms. Kustodiev further remarked: "The arts of Snezhnaya have undergone a profound transformation since Her Majesty the Tsaritsa ascended the throne. What was once the privilege of the aristocracy alone is now shared among the people. Prime Ice sculpture, however, remains a special case. Its unique nature makes it difficult for such works to enter every household. The Veche's decision to hold this exhibition reflects its commitment to Her Majesty's benevolent ideals, as well as its care for the people of Snezhnaya and its equal regard for all."
The Snezhnograd Veche likewise emphasized that an exhibition rich in historical and cultural significance can unite the people and inspire their devotion to Snezhnaya's glory. Thus, even amid these days of fierce winds and heavy snowfall, the decision to hold such an exhibition is considered both worthwhile and necessary.

While the Veche has yet to announce the exhibition's exact date, preparations are already underway. This newspaper has learned that commissions for the exhibition's artworks have been sent to Svetloledovka, where local Prime Ice designers have begun their work. Among them is Malevich, a designer from the town, who told our reporter that he was immensely proud to have been chosen. For him, the significance of this opportunity lies not in any special distinction, but in the fact that he is one of the countless ordinary people of Snezhnaya.
<region id = 2/>
<title name = Tales of the Strange and Incredible: A Duke's Confession (Contributor Story)/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_09/>
<center>Tales of the Strange and Incredible: A Duke's Confession (Contributor Story)</center>
To all who read these words, I am Duke Trokhin. My beloved kin, my graceful and cherished wife, my countless servants... all were claimed by the flames. I alone remain, condemned to endure this wretched existence and to record the sins of the one who brought this tragedy upon us.

"Let all who harbor dissent be seized from wherever they conceal themselves. Let each be examined and judged, and let those deemed guilty be removed by whatever means are deemed necessary. Thus is this order given."

Sorin the arsonist carried out the oppressor's command, bringing my family to ruin through the cruelest of means. Their cries rose as the flames consumed them. The fire itself answered with a dreadful melody, while their twisted, blackened forms became a final dance of agony. That vision returned me to the memory of our last gathering...

How I long for that night... While our oppressor slept beneath the cover of darkness, we gathered beneath the same sky and lit the lamps of celebration. We danced... we sang... paying no heed to the bodies oppression had left hardened and unmoving...

And then... the exile came. We were punished for the joy we dared to show, for the dances we shared, for the obedience we abandoned, for the knees we refused to bend. Within that splendid prison, we found solace in one another. We shared our hatred and stood united beneath the shadow of oppression. Yet when we reached the land of exile and the rains began to fall, we became the instruments of our own undoing. We turned against one another, and that became the fire that truly consumed us. Some even came to yearn for the oppressor — for the small sweetness he had once bestowed.

It was only when the flames touched my own body that I finally understood I was about to be consumed by the fire. But why? What terrible offense had I committed? Was it because I no longer wished to bow my poor spine and continue serving as a gentle support for those who sat so proudly above me?

Well... now I stand alone. With no one left beside me, another dance of rebellion is no longer possible. I am only a poor, lonely duke. What else can I do? All that remains is the rest of my life, and I shall spend it remembering the night when we danced together.

<title name = Healthguards, Guard Your Health!/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_02/>
<center>Healthguards, Guard Your Health!</center>
Want to live longer after 40? Start with one simple habit: walking!

The eminent medical expert, Prof. Lobanov, has made a startling discovery that once humans or even fae pass the age of forty, the life essence within their bodies gradually begins to fade. He believes this decline in vitality is the very reason why various ailments begin to appear.

Fortunately, the body itself possesses a secret weapon against the effects of aging.

After all, have you ever stopped to wonder why those who have lived the longest are, without exception, the elderly?

The reason is surprisingly straightforward. They have walked more roads throughout their lives. Therefore, by keeping your legs in motion each day, you too can move closer toward longevity. Even one hour of walking brings you a full sixty minutes closer to a longer life!

Follow Healthguard for more daily health tips!
