<title name = Tales of the Strange and Incredible: Tales of the Strange From Okurov (Contributor Story)/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_10/>
<center>Tales of the Strange and Incredible: Tales of the Strange From Okurov</center>
As everyone knows, a caterpillar spins a cocoon within a leaf and transforms into an ominous moth; the spawn of a frog lies in the muck, eventually sprouting legs to become a leaping, swimming frog. Ancient fae legends even held that when a person died, was buried, and rotted away, their spine would transform into a snake.

The way life begins is always different from how it ends. There is but one bird that proves the exception to that rule.

In the depths of a beautiful valley lives a lovely Firebird, so lovely that none who look upon it can tear their eyes away. Its wings, when spread, are so large they can blot out the sky; its eyes gleam like gemstones, while its feathers dazzle like gold. All who behold it cannot help but follow it deep into the valley, becoming to it beloved nourishment.

Of course, the Firebird does not feast on foul-smelling flesh, but rather upon memories.

The vast palace of Memory is the dwelling place of the soul. Without memory, a person ceases to be human. Once the Firebird devours their memories, they lose their senses, emotions, and speech, regressing into insensate trees that cluster around the valley town, shielding it from outside eyes. And the Firebird needs only wait — to wait for the next curious visitor to draw near.

Of course, time leaves the marks of age upon the Firebird, and sharp blades inflict their wounds. Death is never far from this beautiful creature, yet the promise of new life always favors it. When the breeze blows, its spent shell warms in the sunlight, and the flames of life ignite its magnificent plumage. It beats its wings amidst the searing inferno, while the falling ash nourishes the growth of fresh flesh and blood. Ultimately, the Firebird dons its resplendent attire once more, circling above Okurov, gazing quietly down at every passerby captivated by its beauty.

(Therefore, this writer sincerely recommends that all readers cherish their lives and stay away from Okurov. After all, unlike the Firebird, we only have one life to live!)

<title name = Watch Out for Insurance Scams, Keep Your Mora Safe/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_04/>
<center>Watch Out for Insurance Scams, Keep Your Mora Safe</center>
"Solemn promises at purchase, but not a single Mora paid out during claims"? Rumors regarding Snezhnayan insurance traps have recently been circulating widely. Following an in-depth investigation, our reporters discovered that the cases in question all involve an entity named "Snezhnajoy Insurance."

Last year, a traveler from Mondstadt signed up for insurance with this company and bought "Prime Ice Construct Melt Insurance" for their Prime Ice fishing rod. The policy was as follows: If the insured item were to melt, the beneficiary would obtain up to 200,000 Mora. This traveler then returned to Mondstadt to fish, only for the rod to melt. The traveler went to seek recompense, only for the company to claim that this policy clearly stipulated that "the insured item must be proven to have melted within Snezhnayan borders," and as such, the traveler was not eligible for compensation.

This is not an isolated case. Recently, a Snezhnograd resident encountered claims issues related to this company's insurance products. This citizen, who wishes to remain anonymous, was originally quite an art enthusiast, but has found the Snezhnayan theater scene's output to have become of uneven quality. As such, she purchased this company's "Audience Trauma Insurance." However, when she did indeed view a truly terrible production, resulting in her being unable to drink her favorite Rimecurrant Puree, she attempted to claim compensation, only to be told by the company that to claim this insurance, the policyholder must prove that she genuinely suffered psychological trauma from watching the play, but the fact that she was able to come in person to file the claim indicated that she was mentally sound.

At present, Snezhnograd authorities have already filed an investigation into this company. At the same time, the Transport Bureau would like to remind all Snezhnayan citizens to be on alert against insurance traps and to keep their Mora safe. Additionally, for those who wish to purchase train delay insurance, we ask that you select the official insurance products offered by the Transport Bureau to safeguard your rights and interests.

<title name = Snowland Sensations: The Theory of Historical Echoes (Contributor Story)/>

<center>Snowland Sensations: The Theory of Historical Echoes (Contributor Story)</center>
New Teyvat Chronicles: Snezhnaya (V)
Historical Echoes — Fiction or Science?

In a previous installment, I posited that there are striking similarities between the pseudo-histories mainstream historians firmly believe in and the authentic historical records of Snezhnaya — similarities so profound that they can no longer be explained merely by cultural contact or the transmission of legends.

I want to begin by summarizing this phenomenon as "Historical Echoes": That is to say, documentary records that appear to come from different regions and eras, but which in fact are the same history, albeit repeatedly rewritten from different perspectives — with this hidden history being the chronicle of Emperor Monomakh's conquest.

During Emperor Monomakh's reign, most of Teyvat's regions were, in reality, under the rule of the same Tsardom.

Having read the Adventurers' Guild's reports, all nations today play host to ancient ruins that possess a relatively unified architectural style — that is, similar to that of ruins we have found in Snezhnaya. This is an incontrovertible fact. And this unified civilization, most evidently, was the realm of Emperor Monomakh.

<title name = A New Chapter in The Seven Impossible Mysteries of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire!/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_09/>
<center>The Seven Impossible Mysteries of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire!</center>
The Seven Impossible Mysteries of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire: The Platinum Piece
Chapter 11

...

"Me? My good sirs, what manner of farce is this?" Grand Duke Brahe Trubetskoy swept his gaze — at once amused and perplexed — over the police officers who were swarming around him like flies, fawning over him desperately. "All my servants can vouch for me! I haven't even stepped foot outside my estate these past few days, being occupied entirely with discussing refined Fontainian operas with Mademoiselle Milady de Este. Where on earth would I have encountered this Viscount Shuisky? Why, I haven't even glimpsed his shadow!"

The officers who had intended to curry favor with him were suddenly struck dumb, left only to exchange bewildered glances. Police Chief Duleyev — our most esteemed Chief — hastily removed his hat and recounted, with great care and in full detail, the events that had transpired: how the young Grand Duke had first arrived as Her Majesty's special envoy, how he had instantly seen through Viscount Shuisky’s ruses, how he had confronted the Viscount and knocked him unconscious with a single punch before the man could even draw his pistol, and how he had personally recovered the stolen platinum piece, and in an act of great mercy helped the locals bury the unfortunate Viscountess...

"Ah, that heartless, raving mad beast, that wicked bandit!" The police chief's face was flushed with intense emotion. "He even cut off one of his fingers, that it might allay suspicion of his guilt! He then hid the lost piece in his glove before speaking to us as if nothing had happened! He even went so far as to use some other poor soul's body to fool us, leading us to believe that some more terrifying serial murder was at play behind this case. Archon's sake, we dug through the snowy plains for months trying to crack this case! It was only thanks to your aid, fair Lord, that nothing further went awry..."

"Nothing went awry, you say!? You've all been deceived, you nitwits, you numbskulls!" The Grand Duke — the real one, this time — hurled his porcelain teacup to the ground, unable to contain his rage, roaring like thunder. "That wasn't me! That was that thrice-be-damned master thief, Reed Miller! He disguised himself as me and assumed my name so he could waltz into Shuisky's manor and take that platinum piece, precious beyond price, like one would fish for Mora in one's pocket! Shuisky had you dancing in the palm of his hand, and now Reed Miller's pulled the wool over your eyes... and you call yourselves detectives!?"

"But... But..." Chief Duleyev sweated furiously, unable to speak through the stutters, "Please, My Lord, please calm yourself... That man had your seal..."

"Fool! If some trifling gentry like Shuisky could fashion a platinum piece real enough to fool the eye, do you not think Reed Miller could forge my seal!?" Grand Duke Brahe Trubetskoy cried, incensed. Before, he had already been played all too often by Miller's beautiful female companion, one who named herself "Wagtail." Even the very mention of Miller's name was enough to give him a headache. He was now realizing that he was once again about to be the laughingstock of Snezhnaya. "What the hell are you waiting for? For the Fire-Water to drown your brains? Get out, and get my piece back, damn you all!"

<title name = Snowland Sensations: Ode to the Snowy Plains (Contributor Story)/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_04/>
<center>Snowland Sensations: Ode to the Snowy Plains (Contributor Story)</center>
(Editor's Note: This poem is a gift from Griboyedov of the Snezhnograd Writers' Guild to the Transport Bureau.)

You stretch out along the railway's path,
The white birches grow in your arms,
Oh, snow plains, you appear, so vast—
Endless, towards the horizon you surge!

The morning light shines brightly upon you, golden;
The moonlight by night keeps vigil over you, then falls into your embrace.
O snowy plains, our mother!
You envelop Snezhnaya's hills, you make our rivers flow.

This grace you bestow infinitely upon life,
Iron ore and sweet beets alike you give, fuel that grows upon you.
How shall we repay you? How your gentle generosity moves me!
Like a puny Kristall Bug, I prostrate before you in piety.

Eyewitnesses described him as wearing battered crimson armor and a bizarre mask. Combined with his uncanny swordsmanship, his frightening appearance was reportedly enough to make several victims drop their belongings and flee before he could say a word.
Following a coordinated investigation led by the Criminal Investigation Division and Druzhna patrol units under the personal supervision of Snezhnograd's Police Chief, the culprit was successfully apprehended late last night. The investigation proceeded without interruption, with officers working day and night until the suspect was located inside an abandoned bakery in the Downtown District. When the fully armed culprit attempted to leave the premises to commit another crime, the patrol teams stationed nearby immediately took action and subdued him!
Investigations reveal that the criminal was a licensed merchant from Ritou in Inazuma. Due to an irreconcilable conflict of interest between the mercantile association and the Kanjou Commission in charge of the area at the time, said association was rendered bankrupt two years ago. Unwilling to revert to being a common citizen, the criminal, backed into a corner, stole crimson armor and a sacred blade that had been offered to a local shrine, then fled the country. First, the criminal fled to the border region of Nod-Krai and engaged in rank charlatanry by assuming the status of an Inazuman Samurai. After being exposed by the Curatorium of Secrets, he then sneaked into Her Majesty's sacred capital, Snezhnograd, planning to continue his deceptions. However, after discovering that he could plunder at will by relying on his terrifying attire, the offender repeatedly employed the same tactic. He was eventually apprehended by law enforcement after inciting city-wide panic.
As the criminal is a fugitive, the Inazuman authorities have refused to recognize his expatriate status. As such, he now awaits judgment under Snezhnayan law. For further updates on how this case shall progress, please keep an eye out for the latest news.
<region id = 2/>
<title name = Tartuffe's Snezhnayan Travelogue/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_09/>
<center>Tartuffe's Snezhnayan Travelogue</center>
(Editor's Note: This is a Snezhnayan travelogue written 138 years ago by the Fontainian author Tartuffe. It was later confirmed that this author never once left Fontaine.)
(Another Note: To prevent the reader from being affected by any misunderstandings due to the factually-incorrect content of the original text, the editor has marked out parts of the text that do not conform to Snezhnayan realities, or that might be easily misunderstood.)
...Our great continent hosts a realm favored by ice and snow. Once, it captivated the imaginations of many adventurers, yet the fear of the cold kept them at arm's length along the border. Consequently, the land became a vast, nebulous symbol, so much so that historians began to doubt its very existence. I, too, once gazed upon it from afar, or circled its periphery, until at last I conquered my fear of the unknown. And so I came to behold it. Through the train window, there it lay — Snezhnaya.
No one fears the extreme cold in Snezhnaya, for though the land is swept by endless blizzards, beneath it grow also combustible gems [1]. Humans are only one of the many forms of sentient life here. Even a hunting dog, a cat with its head held high, or even a large tree you happen to pass by might, out of the blue, speak in some ancient, elegant tongue[2].
The habit of drinking coffee is all but nonexistent in this land, for all things on earth can be brewed into fine wine. A certain noble invited me to try a local product known as "Kvass," which has some subtle similarity to Fonta. He told me that some princes of Snezhnograd once considered traveling to the Court of Fontaine, there to take up residence [3], but had dismissed the notion owing to the lack of Kvass in our lands.
...
[1] This should refer to Kristall.
[2] This is the author's one-sided imagination concerning the fae.
[3] This is complete nonsense.
<region id = 3/>
<title name = Today's "On Ice": What Manner of Performance is This?/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_01/>
<center>Today's "On Ice": What Manner of Performance is This?</center>
I recently went to see "The Seabird," staged in Snezhnograd — the worst program I've seen in decades! In terms of its presentation, it is neither a serious saga capable of evoking a sublime sense of grief in the audience nor a farcical comedy that provokes uproarious laughter.
And what, pray tell, shall the audience find in "The Seabird"? The show might hide behind such fanciful phrases as "avant-garde" or "realism," but they are mere smokescreens for the writer's sore dearth of stage proficiency! A hero is the main character, a figure no story should lack. But there are no heroes in "The Seabird." Our protagonists are a cowardly man, and a failure of a woman. They lack any active aspect, being wholly obedient unto fate, as though they were in spirit minor roles, unable to spark an actor's passion for performance.
Additionally, "The Seabird" forsakes all twists and turns worthy of a great work. Tepid progression interspersed with long pauses — that is the structural characteristic of this play. None sacrifice themselves for a noble cause, nor is anyone redeemed. Consequently, this work leaves one with little to discuss, and its plot and themes can be summed up in a mere two sentences.
And ballet! Ballet, the crowning jewel of Snezhnaya, how "The Seabird" has forsaken your hallowed traditions, and for what? The awful excuse known as "avant-garde." Not once does it give us a touching story, only displaying its loose structure, frustrating side characters, and every insignificant fly and insect. Alas! That this work should see the light of day at all brings me great agony indeed.
(Contributor: Trigorin)

volumes.title: Snezhnaya Vestnik
volumes.story:
<region id = 1/>
<title name = Joyful Insurance, for a Joyful You/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_09/>
<center>Joyful Insurance, for a Joyful You</center>
What ails us most on life's long journey is not the sudden, massive blizzard, but the minor spells of "bad weather" that hinder our progress. A train delayed at a critical juncture, for instance, or a Prime Ice tool melting when it is needed — if left unheeded, even the most inconspicuous setback can escalate into a major emotional catastrophe.
That's where Snezhnajoy Insurance comes into the picture. Every seemingly insignificant "spell of bad weather" in your life is our concern, and we offer you such safe harbors on this voyage:
Train Delay Accident Insurance: If your train is delayed due to human-related factors, we will provide a payout equal to 10 times the ticket price.
Prime Ice Melt Risk Insurance: If your Prime Ice tool should melt within Snezhnaya's vast borders, you will receive a maximum payout of 200,000 Mora.
Audience Trauma Insurance: If you take psychological damage from viewing a theater production, you can be reimbursed for your ticket costs following certification.
For more policy categories, you can consult Snezhnajoy Insurance. We provide speedy, reliable, and responsible payouts, all at your service.
<region id = 2/>
<title name = Today's "On Ice": This is the Performance of an Era/>
<image preview name = UI_Img_SnezhnayaNewspaperPage_Pic_01/>
<center>Today's "On Ice": This is the Performance of an Era</center>
Previously, an article by Mr. Trigorin was published in this paper, criticizing the production of "The Seabird." This essay was quite the disappointment — for here we see how a critic's appreciation for deep art might be thwarted by his rigid, conventional views.
Mr. Trigorin's rejection of "The Seabird" on account of its mundanity and lack of heroes instead speaks to one reason why Snezhnayan ballet has failed to make any breakthroughs for many years. People demand only a few heart-stirring scenes, heaping praise only upon a handful of popular actors. Our so-called stagecraft amounts to nothing more than knowing the moments which shall elicit cheers from the audience and then stringing those scenes together into some convoluted tale.
Whether the onstage world is real and complete is not something that figures into the thought of figures in the art world, such as Mr. Trigorin. What "The Seabird" seeks is to shed the artificiality and shallowness of conventional ballet. The "long pauses" — dismissed with such disdain by Mr. Trigorin — that this work embraces constitute its most profound and powerful elements, for such pauses signify the tension, turbulence, and passivity of real life.
We cannot help but sympathize with these intellectuals, trapped as they are by ossified tradition. They deny all new approaches and new material by mere force of habit, even as they grind the courage to explore art into dust through shallow performance. "The Seabird" is a new thing, a thing that belongs to this era. The names of popular actors may be forgotten in times to come, but the truth of this time, which this work preserves, often proves immortal.
(Contributor: Tripolev)

volumes.title: Investigation Notes
volumes.description: Investigation Notes
volumes.story:
How odd. The collapse in this section of the path to the Pale Crown Palace shows signs of having been caused by an artificially-triggered avalanche.
This requires a rather intricate operation, and... to think the Energy Commission would put up such a sign without reporting it to the Transport Bureau...
Something dubious is afoot.
Is someone in the Commission trying to cover something up? Are they trying to tamper with something inside the Palace?
That said, everyone knows that [...] guards the mausoleum within. In any case, I need to report this to Transport Bureau HQ.
As for those brigands who seek to plunder the Pale Crown Palace. I can only hope they have a chance to regret their folly.
Anyway, it's too cold out here. Time to head back.

name: The Alchemist's Notes (I)
description: The Alchemist's Notes (I)

volumes.title: The Alchemist's Notes (I)
volumes.description: The Alchemist's Notes (I)
volumes.story: The Alchemist's Notes (I)

volumes.title: The Alchemist's Notes (II)
volumes.description: The Alchemist's Notes (II)
volumes.story:
...The experiment is complete.
Aksinya believes it finished as per its designated direction, and thus, a success. And indeed, it is a grand endeavor most worthy of praise.
But can this really be called a success?
So-called eternal love... the so-called courtyard of eternal bliss...
Is that is not merely a dead end with neither change nor improvement?

...

What "shared love"? Is this the world she desires, where all shall love all... Yet love should not be such a thing.
If all differences in this world were to disappear, and all were to be blended into one, what would we be "loving," precisely?
There would be nothing to project love outward upon, nor would there be any corresponding entity within to love.
A "love" created by removing the key elements behind love is nothing but a falsehood, an empty shell.

...

The person within the egg is right.
"He" speaks truth. Aksinya has not perceived the terrifying essence of eternal love.
I cannot... allow her plan to come to final fruition. His Majesty Monomakh has passed, but I know she has not given up simply on that account...
Before the time comes, we must stop her. The person within the egg... I agree with "his" plan.
I know, however, that she will one day surely return, breaking free from the shackles of the land of shadows.
When that time comes, I shall prove to her... that love will not be eroded by cold silence, not even in the grand scheme of eternity.

name: Grand Duke Alvis's Notes
description: Grand Duke Alvis's Notes

volumes.title: Grand Duke Alvis's Notes
volumes.description: Grand Duke Alvis's Notes
volumes.story:
...Even after His Majesty's passing, Hvergelmir remains within my control. This, perhaps, is why His Majesty entrusted everything to me while he yet walked amongst us.
An alchemist who knows only to trample life into the mud, a young Snegurochka dissatisfied with her own race, and... *sigh* Aksinya, the Court Jester whom His Majesty coddled all too much...
How could they possibly survive this tumultuous situation on their own?
They will still have to rely on my methods, will they not?

...

Yet we Domovoy were never ones to do business at a loss, Your Majesty, the late, great, Belyi Tsar...
Naturally, I have the means to protect this secret chamber, sitting precariously as it does like an egg in an overturned nest. But all within it shall be mine to claim.
The great sighing in my mind has grown more frequent.
The person in the egg, the creature who was created... dares to lecture me?
Yet "his" words are not bereft of sense.

...

I will have vengeance upon [...], yet this move must not be discovered by the one who sits upon the new throne...
The destruction of Kitezhgrad appears to me a perfect opportunity to avoid the cleansing directed at [...]
Snezhnaya shall need a new Kitezhgrad, and that shall be my great work. Once accomplished, even the one on the new throne shall have no choice but to acknowledge me.
Before that, I should... I shall get the share I deserve. It is what "he" promised to me. I must obtain that power.
And after that, once Novokitezhgrad has been established, we can move Hvergelmir to that new city in secret.
Everything here shall be of aid to my research... All so I can get closer... to that person within my mind...

name: The Ashen Traveler's Notes
description: The Ashen Traveler's Notes

volumes.title: The Ashen Traveler's Notes
volumes.description: The Ashen Traveler's Notes
volumes.story:
Everything in here is a loop... We're constantly repeating the day of the princess's wedding!
How many years have I spent in here? How many years before I realized that this was going on?
Every day, every day, every day...
I would promise her that, once the princess's wedding was over, we would flee this godforsaken mountain mansion together...
Throughout all these many cycles, neither of our feelings have changed, mine or hers. It's just that...
We never left. We were never able to.

...

For the long-lived fae, this daily, grinding torment might be nothing more than the hazy state just before a dream begins to fade.
But as a human, I have already aged...
Perhaps that was how I broke free from the cycle. I had grown too weak...
Will she see my cold body, which has ceased to breathe?
Will my death sadden her?
It will, I'm sure. Even in this deplorable situation, I can be sure that our love for one another burns as bright as ever.
...It is fortunate, then, that this perpetual cycle will cause her to forget about my death.
This way, she can continue living with hope in her heart...
Hah. To think that I have come to be thankful for this everyday cycle.

...

Hah. I can barely even hold my pen anymore. It seems I am about to break our promise.
My poor, dear Aglaya... I hope you can read this letter, and then... forget the name Myshkin...

name: Document With Yellowed Pages
description: Document With Yellowed Pages

volumes.title: Document With Yellowed Pages
volumes.description: Document With Yellowed Pages
volumes.story:
(A yellowed document that seems to have grown quite brittle due to an overly dry environment, written in a cold, stiff hand with almost no variation...)

I have no love for Larisa.
Though she may own all that I own, and possess Prime Ice artisanry equal to mine.
Though she may be my better in ceremonial and etiquette, such that even the previous princess, harshest amongst us, praised her.
Though... all amongst our kin love her, believing her to be noble, elegant, and a perfect fit with all that people imagine a Snegurochka to be.
She is a Snegovik amongst Snegovik, ever so perfect and impeccable.
But I do not like her.

...

A Snegovik's love is a sacrifice, a form of voluntary exchange.
You open your heart and take all from it, then expect the one you love to take all from his and give it to you.
But you, Larisa. The Prime Ice creation skills you have honed, your graceful actions, your gentle words...
Does that all exist for the sake of "sacrifice"? In your everyday life, the sharpening of your arts, in the many moments you spent caring for the flowers... Where were you? Where could you be found in them?
I asked her about this once.
But she was not offended by this question. She simply looked at me with an expression I cannot name, yet one that was almost sad, and said:
"Your heart is sealed, Pavlina. The greatest misfortune that could befall one living in this world is to love no one at all."
But must I sacrifice all for the person I love? If that is the case, then I would rather not love anyone.
The gentle words and sorrowful gaze she turned upon my doubts... all of it angered me.
Indeed, I have no love for her.

...

"The one who leads the Snegovik must have a complete soul."
Such was the instruction of our ancestor, Morevna.
And there is but one way for a Snegovik to possess a complete soul, and that is to seek true love.
Larisa brought her chosen lover back to Hesperides with her, and when by his side, she reveals such vistas of joy heretofore unseen.
Does that really make her so happy?
The decision she made in choosing her lover... Did she make it as part of the path our princess must take...
...Or did it come from the heart?
Many of our kin praise the man by her side. They say he is a handsome human. That they are a fine match, he and Larisa.
But I find him ugly and rude besides. His vulgar behavior is hardly a harmonious pair with her elegance.
When they appear together, I cannot help but feel frustrated, even nauseous.
Her taste, I suppose, must be terrible.
I have never liked those with a poor sense of aesthetics.
I suppose that is why I have never liked Larisa.

...

That man! He deserves it. He deserves it! He deserved to have his flesh and blood flensed from his bones by blades forged from wind and snow alike!
How dare he have second thoughts at this most important of ceremonies! Did he not know that you had sacrificed your life for this, Larsia!?
And yet he fled in the midst of the ritual — that cowardly human filth! That rat! That thief!
You too, Larisa! You who received no reply, you who were so annoying, you who had terrible taste... You deserved this!
But Larisa, oh, Larisa...
Were you ever so furious? Ever so sad?
Behold the clouds, how they stop for you! Even the thunder has been seized by your desire to set all to rights...
If this was the real you, you as you are now, why did you not burst into fury at these ridiculous rules earlier?
Why did you not show forth your wrath at this false "love" that we must offer up?
Why were you not... enraged at me when I doubted you?
Why did your body become so fragile when I raced toward you through the blizzard?
Why were the joy and laughter that once graced your face, indeed all of you, so quickly reduced to snow-foam amidst the frigid winds, like tears...
...And when they fell on my face, why were they no colder than a single drop of icy rain?

...

Later, I ascended to become the princess of the Snegovik. Strange, I say. Most strange. Should not one who leads us be this so-called complete soul?
A truly ancient Snegurochka, one held in high esteem amongst us, looked deeply into my eyes as she held the ceremony and said, "Sometimes, these things also happen."
What does she mean, "these things also happen"!?
If this throne could be inherited without finding true love... what was Larisa's sacrifice for, then!?
How long must our race be bound by these strange rules...
I must find it... I must find a way to resolve this. For the sake of my kin, trapped and bound by this absurdity they call "love."
For...
For Larisa, for whom I held no love.

volumes.title: Okurov Town Sewer System Design Plan
volumes.story:
Foundation trench to be excavated below Okurov, following the valley's natural slope...
...The two side walls of the sewer are to be built from hard stone in a staggered bond, with sufficient thickness to bear the load of the Okurov roadway... Once the walls are of the specified height, an arched centering frame is to be installed over the sewer. Stone blocks are then to be laid symmetrically from both sides toward the center, with a wedge-shaped stone finally inserted at the crown to close the arch...
...
(The construction of the sewer is the heart of the entire project. I will need more "manpower"... Ah, the townsfolk. Once they have built safe havens for their family, friends, and loved ones, I shall give them ██████... And they shall find eternal ████ beneath the earth...)
...
To build a control room.
"Cast aside the old █████, so that ██████ may never again..."
"Cast aside the old █████, so that ██████ may never again..."
"Cast aside the old █████, so that ██████ may never again..."
To create three keys (red, white, and blue) to control and facilitate passage.
...
(Furiosa... Furiosa is a good girl. Not only does she have hope and desire, she is also determined to contribute to the cause... How precious she is! ...She has followed me here just to ██████... I have fulfilled her wish.)
...
...A single channel is all that is needed to drain excess water from the town... At times of rain, the drainage outlet is opened; when there is no rain, the water is stored in a reservoir...
(The gratitude of the townsfolk... And in return, I am grateful for their help... Their ██████, their shared love, binds us together... We are united in ████████, in pursuit of... the same thing...)
...
(Here, we ████████ together.)

volumes.title: Records Left in the Terminal
volumes.story:
The Archaeolune Energy disturbance is growing at an accelerating rate. In severe cases, this can lead to an energy storm. This is a new phenomenon that was not observed at the time of our first arrival on the moon.
Kalag insists the cause is blackbody contamination from Ungien's Circle. The origin, then, naturally lies with Ungien himself, and with the mysterious visitor he brought back from outer space.
Hmph. Kalag may be an imbecile, but not even she would believe that. It is simply not possible that contamination from a single site can cause a power anomaly that has covered almost the entire lunar surface.
She's only saying that because it gives her a reason to remove Maagees' people from the biosphere. And I doubt she is acting alone... King Xiuhcoatl has always favored Ungien and Maagees. Kalag would never have dared to make a move against them without solid backing...
...But that is a matter for another time. For now, the most important thing is to complete the development of the inhibitory field device. This must be done as soon as possible before we end up delaying every other project on the moon.
And one more thing — and yes, I know this is an irresponsible conjecture, but is it possible that the Archaeolune Energy disturbance is actually coming from the Moon Maiden over at the Lunar Palace? The palace sits right over the Moonheart, after all, like a spring above its source...
I hear that one of Maagees' students has been visiting the Lunar Palace rather often recently. If, somehow...
No... I honestly cannot imagine why he would do such a thing...
And certainly not the kind of circumstances that would make the Moon Maiden agree to something like this.

volumes.title: Records Left in the Terminal
volumes.story:
Professor Maagees has successfully operated on Containment Object-1 using an emerging, unproven biotechnology. She has managed to turn it into something completely new: a living being that is the total fusion of Archaeolune Energy and blackbody matter...
That little onyx creature grows bigger with every passing day. Maybe one day it will be even bigger than the sky itself. But we all know that no matter what it becomes, it will never be the Professor Ungien we knew...
I only hope Kalag's security force does not learn of this... Otherwise, even Project Lunar Veil won't be safe from the fallout.
They don't have access to my lab yet, so they shouldn't be looking here... at least for now.

volumes.title: Records Left in the Terminal
volumes.story:
Today, I will bid farewell to Professor Maagees. In accordance with her wishes, I will perform that operation of creation on her later today, just as she once did when she created Ungie.
This is something I have to do myself, for it is what Professor Maagees wants. The experience I gain from the operation will be vital to the upcoming Project Moongazer, particularly to the work of creating life itself. This is also in line with King Xiuhcoatl's wise counsel.
For so long, I believed her insistence on sending that message was simply grief turned into obsession, the fixation of a human being who had lost the one she loved.
But then she showed me the entirety of the message brought by the Stellar Blackbody. It was only then that I finally understood what she had been reaching for.
I understand now, too, why the Eye of Ibni-Belum team chose to stand with her, even if that meant defying Kalag's security force, and even though to the first Moongazers, both she and Professor Ungien were considered traitors...
The pioneer Ibni-Belum once proclaimed to the researchers who had set foot on the moon: "The sky of stars above our heads was born not of the King's dreams. It hath ever been there, mysterious and silent, awaiting the day its children would look up in curiosity..."
Yes, my teachers were much like children of the stars. They loved the starry sky with such devotion that, from where I stood behind them, I could almost glimpse the shape of the universe in their silhouettes.
...
My dear teachers, it has been my honor to spend this time with you on the moon.
Though you are now gone, your will remains. I, Lusalim, your student, will see it carried forth.

volumes.title: Records Left in the Terminal
volumes.story:
Looking back, I have been blessed with three incredible pieces of good fortune in my life.
First, it was truly my good fortune that I was born in the age after Ibni-Belum, for otherwise, I would never have had the chance to reach the moon.
The second piece of good fortune was being taken in as a student by Professors Ungien and Maagees, once learned members of the Moongazers themselves.
And third... I am grateful for you, Ninnin.
Ninnin, you did not come into this world the way we did. You are... a true child of the stars.
That is why I now entrust Project Moongazer, now only one step away from completion, to you. And that final step is — life, information, and memory must be given a way to be inherited and to circulate. The power of the moon's origin, granted to us by the Moon Goddesses, is enough to make this possible.
I will not live to see the project completed, for I have sinned against dragonkind. I capitulated to that terrifying sovereign who was not of this world, and surrendered the precious results of our research... And I do not intend to escape judgment.
But you know very well why I made that choice. You know what it was for... I had my own mission to fulfill.
Now, I believe in you more than anyone. I believe you can finish walking the rest of the road none of us could...
From now on, everything that follows, I place in your hands.
...
I hope that when I am gone, I can journey into the sea of stars. There, I would leave behind a few drops of tears, like cups of wine raised in tribute to my teachers.
Then, I would gather a few stars and set them beneath the curtain of night, to form a single line that says, "The dragons were here."

volumes.title: Chanson of the Boatman
volumes.story:
I am Euthyphro, hailing from Arcadia, the eternal holy city.

O Mother of the silver shuttle, the ever-blessed goddess Prusmene,

By thy grace, I take up this meager quill to chronicle the night's final splendor.

I beseech thee: grant me once more the hallowed gift of inspiration; preserve thy devout believer,

Lest my soul descend beneath the silver tree, to be sullied by the dust.

O wise and radiant queen, bringer of the light!

I beseech thee: deliver thus thy devout believer,

That my mortal frame may find eternal rest within thy holy embrace.

O wondrous Prusmene — ancient mother of the night and daughter who brings the light, mistress of the Golden Hall!

Countless times hast thou guided my vessel, permitting me to usher unsullied souls unto the lunar palace above the clouds.

Thou grantest mortals slumber within thy pale embrace; thou grantest them dreams that are theirs, and theirs alone.

Yet this is to be the final night — the final rest.

For there sits the eternal throne in the heavens, the Primordial One,

O world-shaking lord! It forges the bones of the earth.

It bids all dreams return to the earth, and all dreamless things to return to the earth.

It seeks to shroud the dreams of man with its own dream,

That we, the mortals of this fleeting world,

Shall abide an age without beginning or end,

Passing through a life of tranquil, dreamless rest.

O wise and radiant queen, bringer of the light,

Deliver me from the hands of my dread master!

For thee, I have ushered the unsullied souls,

For thee, I have steered the silver shining ship

I beseech thee: deliver thus thy devout believer,

That my mortal frame may find eternal rest within thy holy embrace!

volumes.title: Ia-Ilimmu Storage Array Index: I
volumes.story:
<color=#FFD780FF>System Log - Non-Public Access Level | Recorder: Nu-ur-Gestug</color>

...

...I have performed some brief deductions. It appears that Professor Maagees... Researcher Maagees-Geti was on the right path after all.

...Mathematically, the conclusion can be formally derived that any system of sufficient complexity is computationally equivalent and possesses an indistinguishable identity in any measurable sense.

...In other words, a self-awareness simulated by a sophisticated mechanical or informational architecture is, by definition, no different from the consciousness of organic life.

...She yearns to reclaim a life from yesterday, yet the result of her realization is the genesis of a life for tomorrow... For her, what could be more ironic?

...

...Researcher Lusalim approached me today with a peculiar proposal.

...Based on their current findings, he claims it is theoretically possible to engrave the full measure of a researcher's affections, desires, and ideals into data. Through the application of (...), these fragments could be manifested as an "immortal life." He does not mean "immortality" in the literal sense — After all, only a madman or a fool devoid of common sense would believe the laws of this universe permit the existence of an eternal, flawless object. Rather, he envisions a life that can re-emerge, infinitely, no matter how many times it is extinguished. Even if its new incarnation no longer bears the form of a dragon...

...In this way, he argues, the ideals of the Moongazers, and the aspirations of Professor Maagees could be broadcast across the ages, just like a certain beam of light drifting through the void for billions of years.

...He intends to name this unborn life "Nin-Kiggia," or messenger. Well, I bet it's nothing more than a whim of pure sentiment.

...I told him plainly that I have no interest. I don't even understand why he chose to confide in me. Are we truly so familiar? Besides, I am a recorder, not a researcher...

...

King Xiuhcoatl paid a visit today. His Highness, with his characteristic gentleness, expressed a profound interest in Researcher Maagees-Geti's theories, noting their parallels to his own ongoing work. He hopes to manifest life through the use of Phlogiston (or what we call computronium), so that our kin upon the surface might find some small relief, and perhaps, a measure of happiness.

...I spoke with the King at length, and I must admit the conversation was most enlightening. However, in a moment of carelessness, I mentioned Researcher Lusalim's plan to him. After a moment's reflection, His Highness offered a wealth of practical, actionable suggestions...

...It truly was a lapse in judgment. I have already begun to regret it. I am a recorder, not a researcher. My exchange with the King was merely a slip of the tongue — I neither can, nor will, nor do I have any desire to provide assistance to Lusalim's project.

...

...Yet, out of professional rigor, I have forwarded the King's suggestions to Researcher Lusalim anyway.

...

volumes.title: Ia-Ilimmu Storage Array Index: II
volumes.story:
<color=#FFD780FF>System Log - Public Access Level | Recorder: Nu-ur-Gestug</color>

...Phase II retrofitting of the orbital positioning facility in Nephilheim — constructed by Moongazer Ibni-Belum, hereafter referred to as "Engraving" — is complete. The data storage array has been successfully mounted.

...Downlink testing from the lunar terminal to the surface receiving node has concluded. Both data throughput and fidelity significantly exceed initial estimates.

...Deployment of this redundant node will effectively enhance the overall structural robustness and fault-tolerance threshold of the storage array. In the event of unforeseen, extreme circumstances resulting in irreversible damage (including but not limited to physical destruction and cognitive contamination) to the primary lunar storage array, subsequent researchers will retain access to the backup storage array in Nephilheim, ensuring the lossless retrieval and recovery of core research results.

...The original "Engraving" has been reinforced. Countermeasure testing against (...) and (...) weapon systems has concluded. For detailed records, refer to the appendix. Despite its original design intent, the facility is capable of serving as an emergency bunker.

...May the Creator be forever crowned with supreme glory.

volumes.title: Ia-Ilimmu Storage Array Index: III
volumes.story:
<color=#FFD780FF>System Log - Non-Public Access Level | Recorder: Nu-ur-Gestug</color>

...Researcher Maagees-Geti... Professor Maagees's condition is not improving.

...I am so deeply restless, and my recording duties have suffered terribly because of it. Lusalim says that the word has reached King Apep, and she has already sent her finest physicians... But what is the point? If even the three Moon Sisters left behind by Father Nibelung cannot reverse the erosion of the soul itself, what could the Lord of Dendro possibly do...

...To take my mind off from this sorrow, I went to ask around about Lusalim's Project Moonveil. It turns out his design is as conventionally uninspired as ever.

...He honestly think hiding our world under a false veil will keep the Dark Destroyer from noticing us?

...It is utterly idiotic. Under King Xiuhcoatl's rule, even a three-year-old dragonling — once dipped in phlogiston — knows that this kind of self-delusion does nothing more than buy a little time before the inevitable doom arrives...

...And how long can it even last? Tens of thousands of years? Hundreds of thousands? On a cosmic scale, what's the difference? This isn't how you save a civilization. It's like hiding a hatchling inside an eggshell. In the end, it either gets sniffed out by a predator or suffocates in its own shell. Do they honestly believe this is some flawless, long-term solution?

...Granted, I am merely a recorder, not a researcher, and I have absolutely no desire to meddle in their designs... But if a better alternative could be found, surely Father Nibelung would be pleased...

...Yes. This is solely for my Father's pleasure...

...

...An idea crossed my mind, though I don't know if it's truly feasible.

...Theoretically speaking, we could alter an observer's fundamental perception through cognitive interference, or rather, a cognitive hazard. If our planet appears to them as nothing more than a mundane, barren rock utterly indistinguishable from any other piece of cosmic debris, they would naturally lose any curiosity to look deeper...

...I will give it a try. If this can actually be achieved...

...

...Failure. A complete and utter failure in principle.

...After exposing the subject (a deliberately hideous, colossal statue of Lusalim) to cognitive contamination, the test participant, Researcher Nin-Kiggia, successfully accepted it as a perfectly normal part of my laboratory. When I pointedly asked for her thoughts on the statue of her father, she looked entirely baffled and asked in return, "Isn't it normal for Uncle Nuur to have a statue in his lab?"

...And yet, she immediately realized the subject was abnormal the moment she left the laboratory, and proceeded to beat me with a stick.

...She told me to focus on some actual work. I was focusing on actual work. Lusalim, look at the daughter you raised.

...Even so, this experiment proves one thing... For cognitive interference to work within a specific area, the fundamental principles of perception — the natural order that governs common sense — must first take root across the entire region.

...To make something's existence pass for common sense within a world, and thus stifle any curiosity to look deeper, the foundational laws of reality must first pervade that world. Scaling this boundary up to the entire universe, however, would require those laws to span the entire cosmos. Naturally, the latter is utterly impossible.

...

volumes.title: Greenhouse Research Log (I)
volumes.story:
Day 1: The surface of Containment Object-1 is glossy black. Its morphology remains indeterminate and exhibits irregular wave-like fluctuations. Tests produced no response to auditory, visual, or physical stimuli. No food or water intake was observed today.

Day 30: Containment Object-1 vibrated at a high frequency when shown starfield footage with visible celestial bodies for around ten seconds. The corresponding frequency band has been entered into the spectrometer.

Day 37: The Eye of Ibni-Belum team has decoded the vibration frequency. To our surprise, it was a message in our language... Roughly translated, it reads: "I'm glad this message reached you." Ungie... Is that really you? What are you trying to tell us???

Recorded by: Maagees-Geti

volumes.title: Greenhouse Research Log (II)
volumes.story:
Day 89: Containment Object-1 began to exhibit rapid deterioration after emitting decodable information for nearly a month, and various physiological indicators have now reached critical levels. Immediate extraction of medullary tissue is required in order to identify a possible means of recovery.

Day 92: The medullary tissue extracted from Containment Object-1 consists of black variegated, filamentous ejecta that exhibit the characteristics of an information-bearing organism. I have named this substance "blackbody matter." It is this substance that drives the vibrational transmission of information by Containment Object-1.

Day 98: Phase I experiments confirm that pure energy increases blackbody matter activity, and in particular, the Archaeolune Energy contained in biological organisms produces a stronger response...
Ungie, maybe this is why you ended up like this. That thing you found, it thirsts for our bodies...

Recorded by: Maagees-Geti

volumes.title: Greenhouse Research Log (III)
volumes.story:
Day 107: Professor Maagees has fallen into a coma — it has just come to my knowledge that she had been using her own body to feed Containment Object-1... She's out of her mind. That thing isn't Professor Ungie anymore... I will be taking over the research from here on.

Day 137: Damn it... that knuckle-dragger Kalag has taken control of the biosphere. She's actually blaming our loss of control over the Moonlit Vines on so-called blackbody contamination "caused by Professor Maagees' misguided research" ... The idiocy! Who gave her permission to be here? Did one of the kings decide that our ideas are no longer worth supporting?

Day 138: The biosphere is no longer safe. There is an enemy among us. Containment Object-1 is to be transferred to another location today.

Recorded by: Lusalim
